sections.label: Automation and robotics funding support
sections.summary: The passage states the Automation Support Package and National Robotics Programme are necessary bold moves, and calls the enhanced Risk-sharing Financing Scheme and upsized Mezzanine Growth Fund useful enablers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The $400 million Automation Support Package and the $450 million National Robotics Programme are necessary bold moves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The enhanced Risk-sharing Financing Scheme to support scale-ups as well as the upsized Mezzanine Growth Fund to support expansion and internationalisations are useful enablers.

sections.label: National Trade Platform open innovation
sections.summary: The passage states that developing the National Trade Platform into an open innovation platform incorporating third-party apps and value-adding services is accretive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: To this end, developing the National Trade Platform into an open innovation platform where third-party apps and value-adding services can be incorporated is accretive.

sections.label: SG-Innovate and Launchpad infrastructure
sections.summary: The passage supports setting up SG-Innovate as soft infrastructure and a second Launchpad @ Jurong Innovation District as hard infrastructure for entrepreneurs and researchers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: We need to place-make the ecosystem with the necessary players, the budding entrepreneurs, mentors, venture and private equity funds, among others.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Hence, I fully support the set-up of the new entity SG-Innovate, which is the soft infrastructure needed to foster innovation and collaborations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: On the other hand, we will also need the second Launchpad @ Jurong Innovation District (JID), which is the hard infrastructure to serve as spaces for entrepreneurs and researchers to design and test-bed their new ideas.

sections.label: HDB and IDA smart work centres
sections.summary: The passage suggests HDB could work with the Infocomm Development Authority to set aside shop spaces as smart work centres for heartland startups.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Perhaps, HDB can work with the Infocomm Development Authority (IDA) to set aside shop spaces as smart work centres for Page: 18 heartland startups as well.

sections.label: Transforming construction, manufacturing, logistics sectors
sections.summary: The passage states the Finance Minister mentioned it could be widely applied to transform sectors such as construction, manufacturing and logistics to provide solutions to SMEs at reasonable cost.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The Finance Minister mentioned that it could be widely applied to transform sectors, such as construction, manufacturing and logistics, with the aim of providing solutions to small and medium enterprises (SMEs) at reasonable cost.

sections.label: LEAD+ programme and TAC support
sections.summary: The passage states the LEAD+ programme is the needed boost for TACs, and applauds seconding up to 20 public officers to interested TACs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Of course, the TACs would also need a little incentivising as well, and, hence, the Local Enterprise and Association Development-Plus (LEAD+) programme is the needed boost.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Here is where the Government could encourage the setting up of umbrella TACs to coordinate for the entire sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I applaud the move to second up to 20 public officers to interested TACs to better understand the needs of businesses and to build closer rapport.

sections.label: Integrating economic agencies' scope
sections.summary: Agencies have been effective, but the scope of their work must be examined for better integration, overlap removal and possible re-missioning.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Agencies like the Economic Development Board (EDB), SPRING, International Enterprise (IE) Singapore, A*STAR, JTC, WDA, IDA, among others, have been excellent and effective organisations in carrying out their respective missions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: But as we press on for a decisive shift in our economic growth strategy, we have to examine whether the scope of work of different agencies can be better integrated, and whether we can eradicate overlaps and re-mission the agencies if necessary.

sections.label: Budget payouts, NIRC and surplus
sections.summary: Wage Credit Scheme, SEC and tax rebate put money into businesses, while higher NIRC funds the basic deficit and the surplus may raise spending expectations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The $1.9 billion Wage Credit Scheme payout this year, the $1 billion extension of the Special Employment Credit (SEC) and the enhanced corporate income tax rebate, among others, actually put money into businesses and would help the cash flow position of companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The NIR contribution (NRIC) of $14.7 billion, versus $9.9 billion in financial year (FY2015), helps to fund the basic deficit of $7.7 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: While the overall surplus of $3.45 billion may be good news, it may pose potential problems to the Finance Minister.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I am sure expectations will rise for the Government to spend more, given the surplus that we have.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: However, we should note that the increase in NIRC, which is the major balancing item for the Budget, is merely due to changes made to the NIR framework last year.

sections.label: CEOs on business self-reliance
sections.summary: In a poll, 69% of CEOs think businesses should be more self-reliant and less reliant on Government, though the SBF position paper suggests otherwise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: From the poll, 69% of CEOs think that businesses should be more self-reliant and rely more on themselves and less on the Government to grow their businesses, although I must add that the recent position paper published by the Singapore Business Federation suggests a different sentiment.

sections.label: Technology, jobs and skills mismatch
sections.summary: A US survey showed 47% of existing jobs could be replaced by technology, and shortened product lifespans may create a skills mismatch.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: A recent survey showed that in the US, close to 47% of the existing jobs could be replaced by technology or digitisation in the next few years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The advances of technology and the Internet have created innovative business models which, in turn, caused products and services to become outdated very fast and their lifespan shortened.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: This means that the existing skills of workers may not meet the demand of the new jobs, creating a mismatch problem.

sections.label: Proactive approach to helping workers
sections.summary: Despite comprehensive packages, helping workers can adopt a more proactive, caring and inclusive approach.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Although we have some comprehensive packages, I believe that, in helping the workers, we can adopt a more proactive, caring and inclusive approach.

sections.label: Three economic philosophy principles
sections.summary: The economic philosophy guiding the economy can be condensed to three principles: self-reliance, openness, and remaining updated and relevant.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In my opinion, the principles which characterise the economic philosophy that has guided our economy to its current level of development can be condensed to three basic ones.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: These are self-reliance, openness and a determination to remain updated and relevant.

sections.label: Budget policy innovations for Singapore
sections.summary: The Budget strengthens commitment to principles and introduces subtle policy innovations expanding options for managing Singapore as an advanced economy.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The approach taken in this Budget will, I believe, strengthen our commitment to these same principles.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: What it has done is to introduce subtle policy innovations which will expand the options available for managing Singapore as an advanced economy.

sections.label: National Wages Council 1972
sections.summary: The National Wages Council was set up in 1972 as a tripartite body.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: An early one was the setting up of the Page: 23 National Wages Council in 1972 as a tripartite body.

sections.label: Past Governments and labour market
sections.summary: Past Governments did not rest on their laurels despite the outstanding performance of the labour market.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Despite the outstanding performance of the labour market, past Governments did not rest on their laurels.

sections.label: Deferred and frozen foreign worker levies
sections.summary: Levy increases for S Pass and Work Permit holders were deferred, and the freeze for manufacturing and marine and process sectors was extended.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Last year, in response to the slowing economy, previously announced levy increases for S Pass and Work Permit holders were deferred for all sectors.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In justifying the freezing of levy increases for manufacturing for two years, then-Finance Minister Deputy Prime Minister Tharman drew a link to the "progress in productivity" improvement that had been achieved.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This year, the Finance Minister cites the moderating demand for Work Permit holders in the marine and process sectors in support of extending the freeze on levy increases for another year.

sections.label: Labour market contradictions and complaints
sections.summary: Some observed labour market problems could be manifestations of contradictions, including complaints that local workers are hired mainly to justify DRC-based eligibility for foreign hirings.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Some of the problems we have observed in the labour market could be manifestations of these contradictions.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: There have been complaints about situations where local workers are hired mainly to justify DRC-based eligibility for foreign hirings.

sections.label: Expanding options for weak Singapore Core
sections.summary: It asks whether policy options could be expanded for employers with a weak Singapore Core whose short-term prospects are constrained by supply realities.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Moving forward, would it be possible to expand the policy options for dealing with employers who have a "weak Singapore Core" of workers and whose prospects for moving towards a "stronger Singapore Core" in the short term are actually constrained by the realities of supply?

sections.label: Expansion of SEC
sections.summary: The Finance Minister is expanding SEC for three years up to end-2019 in this Budget.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In this Budget, the Finance Minister is expanding SEC for three years up to end-2019.

sections.label: Wage support for retrenched workers
sections.summary: The speaker hopes the Finance Minister reconsiders expanded wage support for retrenched workers and ties support to conditions like job search.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In a time of disruptive change, it may be better to ensure that the mechanisms for the market-driven reallocation of resources are allowed to function normally than to be slowed.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: That is why I hope the Finance Minister will reconsider his promise under the Adapt and Grow Initiative of expanded wage support for retrenched workers.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: What I would urge him to do is to tie any support to specific conditions, such as the job search process.

sections.label: Singapore R&D spending
sections.summary: Singapore's R&D spending as a percentage of GDP ranked behind several countries, at around 2% in 2012.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: If we look at R&D as an example, in terms of R&D spending as a percentage of gross domestic product (GDP), it is well-known that Singapore ranks behind a number of countries.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In 2012, the figure of around 2% for us was half that of world leaders Israel and the Republic of Korea.

sections.label: Budget prioritises restructuring
sections.summary: The Budget's choice to prioritise restructuring over shorter term concerns is difficult and courageous, fortifying Singapore for the journey ahead.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Thanks to them, Singapore is today a thriving metropolis, with the luxury of fully-financed plans chasing after limited manpower and tight space.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: With virtually no more derelict structures to tear down, we have to choose which good buildings should make way for even newer infrastructure whenever we contemplate a make-over.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The choice in this Budget to prioritise restructuring over shorter term concerns has been a difficult one.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is a courageous decision that will fortify us for the journey ahead.

sections.label: Thriftiness in fiscal policy
sections.summary: Thriftiness laid the cornerstone of Singapore's fiscal policy for 57 years, living within means and saving for a rainy day.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Not surprisingly, this sense of thriftiness laid the cornerstone of Singapore's fiscal policy for the past 57 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: This translated into a fiscal policy where we always live within our means and put away as much as we can for a "rainy day".

sections.label: Government schemes examples
sections.summary: ComCare, Workfare, MediShield Life, Pioneer Generation Package, SkillsFuture and Silver Support Scheme are examples of Government actions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: ComCare, Workfare, MediShield Life, the Pioneer Generation Package, SkillsFuture, Silver Support Scheme are just a few examples of what the Government has done over the years.

sections.label: Long-term benefit for Singapore
sections.summary: The Budget centres on long-term benefit for Singapore, with training schemes, an Industry Transformation Programme and possible pain from restructuring.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: The yardstick being that any decision must centre around whether something is good for the long-term benefit of Singapore − to ensure that it not only benefits us but is enduring enough to benefit successive generations of Singaporeans − our children and grandchildren.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: This is further accentuated by the fact that a significant portion of our Budget initiatives goes to "training or upgrading" schemes, such as SkillsFuture, the Adapt and Grow initiative and the Tech Accelerator programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: This Budget also launches a new Industry Transformation Programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: This is, again, a future-centric programme for the long-term benefit of our economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: But as with all restructuring exercises, we must expect pain when excess is trimmed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Firms should also not expect such grants to be permanent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   In this Budget, the Government also launched the Industry Transformation Programme.

sections.label: SME help and long-term solutions
sections.summary: Corporate income tax rebate, SEC and the SME Working Capital Loan Scheme aim to help SMEs, and the Budget seeks long-term solutions to long-term issues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Higher corporate income tax rebate, SEC and the SME Working Capital Loan Scheme are further initiatives aimed at helping our SMEs succeed amid tough economic conditions and tight labour constraints.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Page: 29 Mdm Speaker, this Budget aims to provide and implement long-term solutions to long-term issues.

sections.label: Urgent economic transformation and productivity
sections.summary: Productivity has been lacklustre, so economic transformation is urgent and structural and strategic reforms must proceed despite cyclical pain.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Page: 30 Our productivity overall, minus the cyclical rebound, has been lacklustre in general.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: This is why I agree with Minister Heng that economic transformation for us is not only critical; it is urgent.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: There is no time to lose and a soft economy should not lull us into slackening our resolve.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: We must press ahead with structural and strategic reforms even as we tackle cyclical pain and strain.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: If we just march on the spot and productivity continues to be lacklustre, then other countries will surely catch up with us, close the distance and then, eventually, overtake us.

sections.label: Local workforce peak around 2020
sections.summary: Government projections state that the local workforce will peak around 2020, four years from now.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: According to Government projections, the local workforce will peak around 2020, that is, four years from now.

sections.label: Re-employment age raised to 67
sections.summary: The Government has accepted tripartite recommendations to raise the re-employment age ceiling from 65 to 67.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: First, the Government has earlier announced that it has accepted the tripartite recommendations to raise the re-employment age ceiling from 65 to 67.

sections.label: Measures for hiring mature workers
sections.summary: Measures encouraging employers to hire mature workers include the Wage Credit Scheme, extension of SEC and Enhanced Workfare Income Supplement for lower-wage mature workers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Second, I applaud the numerous measures announced by Minister Heng in encouraging employers to continue hiring mature workers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: These measures include the earlier announced Wage Credit Scheme, the payouts have just been made, the extension of SEC as well as Enhanced Workfare Income Supplement to lower-wage mature workers, so that more may choose to remain in work.

sections.label: Sectoral Tripartite Committees manpower plans
sections.summary: The 25 Sectoral Tripartite Committees are deliberating and devising Sectoral Manpower Plans to support capability-building and development of their industries.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Page: 32 The 25 Sectoral Tripartite Committees (STCs) are now deliberating and devising Sectoral Manpower Plans to support the capability-building and development of their respective industries.

sections.label: Tapping mature workers' contributions
sections.summary: Efforts to help workplaces appreciate and tap mature workers' contributions must be stepped up, including refining funding programmes like WorkPro and spurring age management methods.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Fourth, efforts to enable workplaces to appreciate and fully tap contributions of mature workers must be stepped up.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: These include not only how to refine funding programmes, such as WorkPro, but also how to spur the adoption of successful age management methods.

sections.label: Building a great metropolis
sections.summary: The passage states that pressing on will build a great metropolis in 20 years, and it is up to us to get it right.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: If we press on, in 20 years, we shall build a great metropolis, worthy of a hardy, resilient and stout-hearted people." He is right.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: And it is now up to us to get it right and show that we can make it.

sections.label: RIE 2020 research funding
sections.summary: $19 billion is set aside over five years for science and technology research under RIE 2020, with $4 billion for industry-research collaboration and $1.5 billion topped up to the NRF.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: An amount of $19 billion has been set aside over the next five years for investment in science and technology research under the Research, Innovation and Enterprise (RIE) 2020 plan.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Under the plan, $4 billion has been earmarked for industry-research collaboration.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Government is further topping up another $1.5 billion to the National Research Fund (NRF) in this Budget.

sections.label: UK R&D return rates
sections.summary: A UK government report estimated median private returns to R&D of around 20%-25%, with social returns typically two to three times larger and public R&D social returns around 20%.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Page: 34 A recent report for the United Kingdom (UK) government estimated the median private rates of return to R&D investments are around 20%-25% in terms of economic output or productivity increases, and social returns are typically two to three times larger than private returns.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In the UK, public R&D investments have yielded social returns of around 20%.

sections.label: Value of R&D for Singapore
sections.summary: The passage questions whether R&D captures economic and social value for Singapore and Singaporeans, citing an invisibility cloak's distant industrial application and a Singapore PR professor's junior role.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: But does it capture the economic and social value of R&D for Singapore and Singaporeans?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: It was a good scientific advance, but industrial application of the cloak is still very far off, as the materials used were bulky and cloaking was effective only from six perspectives.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Beyond the medium-term economic value of R&D for Singapore, another concern is the long-term social value of R&D for Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: It was reported that the research team that invented the invisibility cloak was led by a Singaporean Permanent Resident (PR), a young professor at NTU.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: From the order of names listed as co-authors of the paper of the invention published in a prestigious scientific journal, the Singapore PR professor was listed last and appeared to be a junior member of the team.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The team leader appears to be a Zhejiang University professor who conceived the original idea and led in the design of the cloaks and the experiments.

sections.label: Science park high-tech island
sections.summary: The science park becomes a high-tech island separated from society, with Buona Vista developments including Biopolis and Fusionopolis next to NUS for two decades.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The science park becomes a high-tech island with innovation taking place, separated from the rest of society.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We have had science park developments in the Buona Vista area, including Biopolis and Fusionopolis, next to the National University of Singapore (NUS) for two decades now.

sections.label: Research links with NUS firms
sections.summary: It asks whether formal research links between NUS and firms in science parks are significantly higher than those outside the parks.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Are formal research links between NUS and firms located in the science parks significantly higher than those located outside the parks?

sections.label: Decentralising science parks to heartland
sections.summary: It asks if the Government considered decentralising the industrial district-cum-science park concentration into smaller heartland science parks to tap mass creativity and SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Has the Government considered decentralising the industrial district-cum-science park concentration to seed a network of smaller science parks in the heartland estates, so that innovation can tap on the mass creativity of the Singaporean workforce?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Instead of focusing only on startups, the innovation drive will also plug into the large body of SMEs to enrich our enterprise base and spread innovation to our local companies.

sections.label: Innovation everywhere in Singapore
sections.summary: It states innovation would be everywhere in Singapore, making innovativeness a cultural norm, and hopes the Jurong Innovation District begins a network of innovation estates.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Most importantly, innovation will not be concentrated in two districts but will be everywhere in Singapore, turning the enclaved city into the creative city where innovativeness becomes a cultural norm for everyone in every vocation, from the cleaner to the CEO, from the office clerk to the scientist.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This, I believe, is what Jurong was for Singapore in the 1970s.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I hope the Jurong Innovation District is just the beginning to create a network of innovation estates all over the island, across the city, through the heartland.

sections.label: FY2016 total expenditure increase
sections.summary: For FY2016, total expenditure is $5 billion more than the previous one.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: For FY2016, our total expenditure is $5 billion more than the previous one.

sections.label: Wage Credit Scheme payouts
sections.summary: Over 95,000 employers will receive about $1.9 billion in Wage Credit Scheme payouts by month's end, with SMEs getting about 70%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: In terms of wages and productivity, more than 95,000 employers in Singapore will receive about $1.9 billion in Wage Credit Scheme (WCS) payouts by the end of this month and SMEs will be the beneficiaries of about 70% of the disbursed payouts.

sections.label: SEC extension to 2019
sections.summary: SEC has been extended until 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: SEC, which has been mentioned by a number of speakers before me, has been extended till 2019.

sections.label: PIC scheme claims and changes
sections.summary: The PIC cash payment rate is lowered and the scheme will not be extended beyond Year of Assessment 2018, with 142,000 claims in 2015.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: As the hon Member Assoc Prof Randolph Tan mentioned, sometimes well-meaning policies may not be wise when placed in the hands of unscrupulous employers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I also welcome the lowering of the cash payment rate under the Productivity and Innovation Credit (PIC) scheme and the scheme will also not be extended beyond the Year of Assessment 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The PIC scheme saw 142,000 claims in 2015, more than double the claims in 2014.

sections.label: Kenny Yaps and Revitalisation of Shops
sections.summary: The speaker wishes for more Kenny Yaps and welcomes the Enhancement to Revitalisation of Shops Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I guarantee you that." My only wish is that there are many more Kenny Yaps out there who would do us proud with their conscientious and competitive approach to business.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I also welcome the Enhancement to Revitalisation of Shops Scheme.

sections.label: HDB shop space and SkillsFuture
sections.summary: HDB shop space is becoming a battleground for established brands while local merchants are priced out, and SkillsFuture is one of the Government's best initiatives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: While we can revitalise shops, spruce them up, what is still of concern is how HDB shop space is fast becoming another battleground for established brands selling the same generic stuff, while local merchants, small specialised merchants who have been there for many years, are being priced out by the competition.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Investing in SkillsFuture has been one of the best initiatives that our Government has undertaken.

sections.label: Silver Support Scheme monthly enhancement
sections.summary: It was suggested at the dialogue that the Silver Support Scheme be enhanced to benefit the elderly monthly rather than quarterly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: At the same time, it was also suggested at the same dialogue that the Silver Support Scheme be enhanced to benefit the elderly on a monthly basis, rather than on a quarterly basis.

sections.label: Flat costs and Fresh Start criteria
sections.summary: The speaker hopes flat costs stay low and wants more details on criteria for the Fresh Start Housing Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I hope that the cost of these flats could be kept low to allow them to regroup and move forward.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: We would also need more details on the criteria to identify these families that qualify for the Fresh Start Housing Scheme.

sections.label: Industry Transformation Programme sector teams
sections.summary: Government will set up teams from EDB, SPRING, IE, A*STAR and WDA to develop road maps for each economic sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Minister Heng Swee Keat announced that in order to support the Industry Transformation Programme and strengthen the coordination among Government agencies, the Government will be setting up teams comprising officials from EDB, SPRING Singapore, IE Singapore, A*STAR and WDA, to develop road maps for each economic sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I hope that when Government officials gauge industry potential, they should not only measure the pace of growth and economic contributions but also consider the social functions as well.

sections.label: Enterprise collaboration and $4.5 billion programme
sections.summary: Collaboration among enterprises, TACs and Government agencies matters, and Budget rolled out a $4.5 billion Industry Transformation Programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In this regard, collaboration among enterprises, as well as the close partnership among enterprises, TACs and Government agencies, is of great importance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I really hope to see that the Government could obtain an in-depth understanding of industry development processes and needs, to avoid wrongly interpreting the situation and trends during the process of structural adjustments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: To the officials, any small misinterpretation is just a concept, but, to the enterprises, it is tantamount to wasted time, manpower and resources, which may not be reversed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In this year's Budget, the Government has rolled out a $4.5 billion Industry Transformation Programme to help enterprises.

sections.label: Building up the PPT model
sections.summary: During economic restructuring, the PPT model should be built to integrate Government, enterprises and trade associations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: During this period of economic restructuring, we need to build up the PPT model, and fully optimise the strengths and advantages of the Government or "Public", enterprises or "Private" and trade associations or "TAs", integrating all kinds of ideas, concepts and methods.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In this way, transformation and driving up productivity would not only be the objective of the Government, but also the common target of the Government, enterprises and trade associations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: With this common goal, the effectiveness of the implementation process would be greatly improved.

sections.label: NTUC Place-and-Train programmes
sections.summary: Since 2008, NTUC has worked with industry partners to create over 50 Place-and-Train programmes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Since 2008, NTUC has worked with various industry partners to create over 50 Place-and-Train programmes.

sections.label: Redundancy of workers in their 40s
sections.summary: MOM's 2015 report shows residents aged 40 to 49 formed 33% of redundant residents, and displaced mature PMEs take longer to find employment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: According to the Ministry of Manpower's (MOM's) 2015 Labour Market Report, residents aged 40 to 49 formed 33% of the total number of residents made redundant in 2015.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: This clearly reflects a trend whereby workers in their 40s are more vulnerable and susceptible to job displacement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: On top of that, mature professionals, managers and executives (PMEs) above the age of 40 who are displaced often take a longer time to find employment.

sections.label: SkillsFuture and worker upskilling
sections.summary: SkillsFuture lets workers pick up new skills, and tripartite partners need to articulate future skill sets and help workers upskill ahead of time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The SkillsFuture programme presents a good platform for our workers to pick up new skills and we need to encourage more to make good use of their SkillsFuture credits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The Labour Movement is driving it together with MOM and I would like to ask the House to do more to Page: 44 emphasise such a need to all our workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: But we must be mindful that there will be workers who will be affected in this transformation process.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Singaporeans are most concerned about their job security.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The tripartite partners also need to work closely to articulate the future skill sets and competencies needed for the future jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: We need to help our workers upskill, reskill or second skill – however we call it – ahead of time, instead of in present time or, worse still, behind time.

sections.label: New strategy for Singapore economy
sections.summary: The passage states there is an urgent need for a new strategy, paradigm and narrative for Singapore so Singaporeans can continue to enjoy good jobs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The question is not just about the current headwind but what our future economy is going to be like.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: There is an urgent need for a new strategy, a new paradigm, a new narrative for Singapore so that Singaporeans can continue to enjoy good jobs.

sections.label: Singapore as mitochondria to world
sections.summary: The passage states that Singapore can be the mitochondria to the world.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Singapore can be the mitochondria to the world.

sections.label: Singapore as UN Asia HQ
sections.summary: The passage argues Singapore should host the UN Asia HQ and WHO diagnostic laboratories and disease surveillance centre, citing its infrastructure, workforce and relationships.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Singapore should be the best venue for UN to consider building its Asia HQ as the shift in economic and military power tilts towards our region.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: We have the infrastructure – from transport to communication, from political stability to social security – and with our educated workforce and our close relationships with many countries, Singapore should be the UN regional HQ for Asia.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Likewise, the World Health Organization (WHO) should set up the most advanced diagnostic laboratories and disease surveillance centre here to monitor epidemics and pandemics that can affect the whole world.

sections.label: UN bodies and defence posturing
sections.summary: The passage states UN bodies here would help balance defence posturing, noting Singapore ranks second in military expenditure per capita after Saudi Arabia.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The presence of UN bodies, including the UN Security Council, here would also help to balance our defence posturing.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: We are ranked second in a list of countries by military expenditure per capita, second only to Saudi Arabia.

sections.label: Jokowi Indonesia defence budget pledge
sections.summary: The passage cites President Jokowi's pledge to raise Indonesia's defence budget to 1.5% of GDP from 0.8% for a Minimum Essential Force by 2024.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Take, for example, Indonesia President Jokowi's campaign pledge to increase Indonesia's defence budget to 1.5% of gross domestic product (GDP) from its current 0.8% as Jakarta seeks to achieve a so-called Minimum Essential Force by 2024.

sections.label: Workfare, SkillsFuture and Silver Support
sections.summary: The passage calls WIS and SkillsFuture commendable and caring, and likes Silver Support, which helps the lower 20th to 30th percentile elderly.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) and the investment in SkillsFuture are commendable efforts and, indeed, reflective of our caring policies.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I like the Silver Support Scheme, which is designed to help the lower 20th to 30th percentiles of the economic group of the elderly.

sections.label: Elderly housing scheme eligibility
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the scheme is sustainable and whether capping housing types at 4-room HDB flats is needed given other criteria.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Can we sustain such a scheme, given that our working population to senior citizens ratio is dropping rapidly each decade?

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I have also received feedback from a few upset elderly who own 5-room HDB flats and were excluded from the scheme.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Since there are already two other criteria – per capita income of less than $1,100 and also the CPF contribution limit of $70,000 before age 55, is there a need to cap the housing types only at 4-room HDB flat and below?

sections.label: Businesses learning from crisis
sections.summary: The speaker says local businesses should learn to grapple with crisis and come out stronger rather than receive aid.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This sort of mentality is harmful all round.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: We are encouraging local businesses to venture out, but the business climates in other countries are far harsher than Singapore's.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: There will be more obstacles and nobody will be at hand to provide them with aid and assistance.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: By all means, give them the fishing rod, teach them how to fish, but do not just give them the fish.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The Government and our local enterprises should not waste a good opportunity to learn from a crisis.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Let the businesses learn to grapple with crisis and come out stronger.

sections.label: Expenditure outpacing operating revenue
sections.summary: Expenditure has grown faster than operating revenue for four years, and total expenditure outstripped operating revenue for two years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: For four consecutive years, our expenditure has grown faster than operating revenue growth.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: For the last two years, total expenditure has outstripped operating revenue and this trend may continue, given our ageing population and slowing growth.

sections.label: Industry Transformation Programme
sections.summary: The Budget's central $4.5 billion Industry Transformation Programme targets helping SMEs scale up, use automation and foster innovation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Central to this Budget is the $4.5 billion Industry Transformation Programme, packed with measures mostly targeted at helping SMEs scale up, use automation and foster innovation.

sections.label: Wage Credit Scheme payouts
sections.summary: Firms received $1.9 billion under the Wage Credit Scheme this year to defray wage cost increases for Singaporean employees.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: For example, firms received a total of $1.9 billion under the Wage Credit Scheme this year to help them defray the wage cost increase given to Singaporean employees.

sections.label: Family business succession value loss
sections.summary: A study by Prof Joseph Fan found 65% of family business value is lost from succession issues.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: A study done by Prof Joseph Fan of the Chinese University of Hong Kong found that 65% of the value of family businesses is lost as a result of succession issues.

sections.label: PME foreign hiring scrutiny
sections.summary: The speaker urges labour market tests for employers of foreign PMEs and promoting Hire Singaporeans First, citing PMEs' restructuring burden.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: However, we also need to help our workers cope with the cyclical headwinds and structural changes that will come their way.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: I am especially concerned about the plight of PMEs – they will bear the brunt of economic restructuring, impacting those in their 40s and above the hardest.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Unlike lower-level jobs where foreigners hired on Work Permits and S Passes are subject to dependency quotas and levies, there is nothing similar in place for PMEs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: We need to consider subjecting employers of foreign PMEs to the scrutiny of labour market tests urgently.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: We should not shy away from actively promoting and championing "Hire Singaporeans First", as the Government's first duty is to its own people.

sections.label: Support for displaced PMEs
sections.summary: Employers worry about baggage and motivation when hiring displaced PMEs, so emotional and motivational support must be part of Professional Conversion Programmes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Employers are concerned about having to deal with the baggage and motivational issues that come with hiring a displaced PME.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: We must, therefore, provide the necessary emotional and motivational support to reignite passion, and this must be an integral part of Professional Conversion Programmes.

sections.label: SMEs' share of value-added
sections.summary: SMEs' share of value-added is less than their share of business numbers and employment, and Singapore lacks a mittelstand of world-leading SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Right now, the share of SMEs in value-added in our economy is less than what their share of business numbers and employment would imply.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We lack the equivalent of Germany's mittelstand, a critical mass of world-leading SMEs which are world leaders in niche product categories or technologies, like, for example, Faber Castell, a manufacturer of pencils.

sections.label: Exploit Technologies licensing agreements
sections.summary: From 2004 to 2014, Exploit Technologies signed 920 licensing agreements with private companies, about 80% with SMEs and startups.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Minister for Trade and Industry revealed in response to my Parliamentary Question that from 2004 to 2014, the total number of licensing agreements signed with private companies by Exploit Technologies Pte Ltd, which helps commercialise intellectual property (IP) from the R&D sector, was 920, or just over about 80 a year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Of these, about 80% were with SMEs and startups.

sections.label: Levy rises and support measures
sections.summary: Two sectors face foreign worker levy rises, and the speaker asks whether Budget 2016 measures suffice as PIC support tapers toward 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: These two sectors will see foreign worker levy rises.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: But with PIC support tapering down towards 2018, are the measures in Budget 2016, such as the Automation Support Package and Industry Transformation Initiatives, enough?

sections.label: Unit labour cost versus productivity
sections.summary: From 2010 to 2014, unit labour cost rose 2.15% on average, exceeding labour productivity growth of 0.3% and 1.3%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: For example, unit labour cost for the overall economy increased at an average rate of 2.15% from 2010 to 2014.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This is higher than labour productivity growth of 0.3% measured in terms of real value-added per worker, and 1.3% measured in terms of real value-added per hour worked over the same period.

sections.label: Jurong Innovation District rental costs
sections.summary: Asks whether Jurong Innovation District rentals will suit SMEs and startups or be high and eat into startup funding.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Will the Jurong Innovation District provide a rental cost environment that will be conducive to SMEs and startups which also wish to take advantage of the space, or will rentals be high, eating into their startup funding?

sections.label: Calibrated SME Government support
sections.summary: Says SME Government support such as finance, tax incentives and grants can be more calibrated, with more aggressive support for enterprises that can deliver results.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I think there is far more room for SME Government support, such as access to finance, tax incentives, cash grants schemes and so on, to be much more calibrated, based on the aspirations of SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We can give more aggressive support and higher quantum of incentives and agree on stretch goals with those local enterprises which want it and – this is the crucial point – which can deliver results.

sections.label: STP job matches and internships
sections.summary: In 2015 the Minister for Trade and Industry replied that 155 STP job matches and over 700 STP internships benefited 192 enterprises.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In 2015, the Minister for Trade and Industry replied to Mr Chen Show Mao that 155 STP job matches and over 700 STP internships were implemented, benefiting 192 enterprises.

sections.label: Unlocking talent in scarcity
sections.summary: With talent scarcity and large Public and MNC sectors, more must be done to unlock talent, citing Andy Grove of Intel.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In a situation of talent scarcity, with a large and attractive Public Sector and MNC sector, we must do more to unlock resources of talent, not just because it is the right thing to do morally but also economically.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The late Andy Grove of Intel, for example, was severely hearing impaired as a young man but went on to transform Intel and the global semiconductor industry.

sections.label: SME workers and bosses' planning
sections.summary: Workers hope bosses have detailed planning and improvement to decide whether to stay long term; SME workers are over 70% of the workforce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: They also hope to see that the business bosses have detailed planning and improvement in many areas, and this will help them to decide whether this company is worth staying on for the long term.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: We now know that SME workers account for more than 70% of our workforce.

sections.label: Robotics scheme and job worries
sections.summary: The Minister announced a $450 million robotics scheme, and some people may worry robots will displace work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Second, the Minister has announced a scheme with $450 million on robotics but some people may be worried that the work will be displaced by the robots.

sections.label: LEAD+ scheme for SMEs
sections.summary: The Government introduced a LEAD+ scheme and a website to supply materials and wider capital assistance to SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Fortunately, this year, the Government has introduced a creative scheme, a website, so that all relevant materials Page: 55 will be supplied to SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The Minister has announced this LEAD+ scheme this year which will provide wider assistance in capital and schemes to attract more workers.

sections.label: Earn and Learn Scheme coverage
sections.summary: The Earn and Learn Scheme was introduced last year to attract graduates to SMEs, but industry coverage and quota are small.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Last year, the Government introduced the Earn and Learn Scheme to attract more graduates to join the SMEs but the coverage of the industries is quite small and the quota is small.

sections.label: Mentors and support for SMEs
sections.summary: The Government can send mentors to help SME workers adjust, and the SG100 starting point received Budget support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The Government can also send some mentors to help these SME workers, so that they will adjust effectively to welcome and accept these new contents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The Government and the enterprises should work together with our workers, so that we can move together and overcome these challenges in this uncertain market.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The SG100 starting point has received the strong support of the Budget.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I hope the Statutory Boards and the innovation partners will together be helping our SMEs, so that they can help them to overcome all the challenges they face along the way.

sections.label: RIE 2020 funding allocation
sections.summary: The RIE 2020 Plan allocates $19 billion from 2016 to 2020, with up to $4 billion for industry-research collaboration and a $1.5 billion NRF top-up.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Finance Minister states, again I quote, "The ownership of intellectual property (or IP) allows companies to realise the value of its efforts." The total allocation of funds under the RIE 2020 Plan, from 2016 to 2020, is $19 billion, out of which a sum of up to $4 billion will be directed to industry-research collaboration.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This allocation represents, again I quote the Finance Minister, "a concerted shift towards innovation and enterprise, to capture the economic and social value of R&D." In addition, there will be a top-up of $1.5 billion to NRF this year to support the RIE 2020 Plan.

sections.label: RIE 2020 research flow-through
sections.summary: One of the four major thrusts of RIE 2020 is to strengthen flow-through from research to societal and economic impact.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: One of the four major thrusts of RIE 2020 is to strengthen flow-through from research to its eventual impact on society and the economy.

sections.label: Foreground IP in negotiations
sections.summary: The speaker emphasises being careful in research collaboration negotiations not to concede valuable foreground IP for consolation IP.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The point that I would like to emphasise, hon Members and Madam, is that we must be careful in our research collaboration negotiations not to concede valuable foreground IP in return for consolation IP.

sections.label: Retaining strategic intellectual property rights
sections.summary: The speaker urges clear Government guidelines on retaining strategic IPs from research so Singapore can monetise them and stay competitive.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: That is why we are investing the money, is that not so, so that we can be competitive and profitable?

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We want to be able to monetise such intellectual property rights so that we can receive revenue, whether it be a one-time payment for transfer or recurring revenue by way of royalties and licence fees.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We need to know what to retain and what we concede.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Therefore, I hope that the Government will set clear guidelines for the retention of IPs which are of strategic value to Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We must not let Singapore pay money to be used as a test bed without retaining valuable strategic IPs arising from such research.

sections.label: Patent grants not success measure
sections.summary: The number of patent grants is not a measure of the success of our investments.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The number of patent grants is not a measure of the success of our investments.

sections.label: Funding industry-research collaboration projects
sections.summary: Funding for industry-research collaboration projects should go to the commercial entity or TACs to appoint research institutions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As a corollary, funding for industry-research collaboration projects should be granted to the commercial entity or the TACs for them to appoint research institutions for such purposes.

sections.label: Enabling Village and disability schemes
sections.summary: The Enabling Village opens opportunities for persons with disabilities, and the speaker welcomes the Enhanced Wage Credit, SEC and Workfare Training Support schemes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The opening of the Enabling Village, a one-stop community space and service centre dedicated to integrating persons with disabilities in society, serves to bring new opportunities for persons with disabilities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I welcome the recent Enhanced Wage Credit Scheme and the SEC scheme for persons with disabilities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I welcome the enhancement of the Workfare Training Support Scheme which allows persons with disabilities who earn low wages and are younger than 35 years old to be eligible for funding in their learning.

sections.label: Disability from external internal barriers
sections.summary: A person is disabled by external and internal barriers that impede his development and participation in the community.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A disability – a person is disabled by external and internal barriers that impede his development and participation in the community.

sections.label: National education campaign on disabilities
sections.summary: The speaker asks for a national education campaign so people understand disabilities and can build the country together.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But those are disabilities that are real and hurting.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I ask for a national education campaign so that we can reach out to our people.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I ask that we understand so that we can be one, and I ask that when we understand and when we are one, we can then build a country together.

sections.label: Labour Market Report unemployment figures
sections.summary: MOM's Labour Market Report states Singaporean unemployment rose to 3% in December, with 12,700 long-term unemployed residents in 2015 and about half of redundant workers re-entering within six months.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: According to the Labour Market Report issued by MOM last month, unemployment among Singaporeans rose to 3% in December, meaning that more than 58,000 Singapore Citizens were out of work.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As for long-term unemployment among residents, for those who have been searching for work for more than 25 weeks, for the whole of 2015, there were 12,700 residents in this predicament.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The report further noted that among those made redundant and sought to re-enter the workforce, only about half of them were able to do so within six months.

sections.label: Publishing underemployment and demoralised workers
sections.summary: The Government should use existing data to publish headline numbers including time-based underemployment and demoralised workers who have given up looking for work.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: First, the Government can use the existing data it already collects and publish headline numbers showing not just unemployment, the headline numbers should include time-based underemployment and the numbers of demoralised workers, meaning those who have given up looking for work and, hence, dropped out of the unemployment statistics.

sections.label: Adapt and Grow target groups
sections.summary: Adapt and Grow is stated to target those facing greater difficulty finding jobs and mid-career jobseekers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Adapt and Grow is stated to be targeted at those who face greater difficulty in finding jobs and for mid-career jobseekers.

sections.label: Feasibility of redundancy insurance
sections.summary: The Government should study introducing redundancy insurance funded by small worker and employer contributions, paying 40% of last drawn salary for six months to involuntarily unemployed workers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To this end, the Government should look into the feasibility of introducing redundancy insurance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: One model could involve requiring workers resident in Singapore and their employers to each contribute a very small percentage of the employee's monthly salaries towards a fund.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The fund should be geared towards helping workers who undergo involuntary unemployment, meaning those who are made redundant, including those terminated with notice.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The fund could gear towards giving a six-month payout at a fraction of the worker's last drawn salary, say, 40%, subject to a cap, say, based on the median wage.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Such a modest scheme of limited payouts which end after six months will send a clear signal that only a temporary buffer is being provided, incentivising the worker to actively prepare to earn his own income again.

sections.label: Growing the pie for social spending
sections.summary: The sustainable solution for social spending is to grow the pie, with Budget measures to transform the economy and a suggestion to upgrade the Singapore Inc model.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The sustainable solution to provide more resources for social spending is thus to grow the pie so that we have more to share.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Page: 64 The scale of the issues that confront restructuring economies worldwide is not lost on us, and while the Minister for Finance urges us not to let pessimism take hold in the midst of difficult conditions, the need to act decisively and quickly is apparent, as he said, and I quote: "The global economic landscape is changing and our challenges are pressing.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: We must find every opportunity to transform, to emerge stronger in the coming years." The Budget contains a host of measures to hasten the transformation of our economy – the Automation Support Package, Financing and Tax Incentives to Support Scale-ups and even a Business Grants Portal to streamline grant applications for our firms.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In our policies to grow the economy, we should also emphasise demand-pull policies – policies that help create new markets and expand existing ones – and I would like to suggest that we can do this by upgrading the Singapore Inc model.

sections.label: Singtel investment in Trustwave
sections.summary: Singtel's investment in Trustwave is an example of companies growing competencies via M&A and internationalising into new market segments quickly.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Singtel's recent investment in Trustwave, the largest independent provider of cybersecurity services in North America with a presence in Europe and Asia, is an example of how our companies can grow Page: 65 competencies via M&A and internationalise in new market segments quickly.

sections.label: Uber company value five years ago
sections.summary: Uber was a $60-million company five years ago.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: To give some examples, Uber was a $60-million company five years ago.

sections.label: Uber growth and company expansion
sections.summary: Uber grew to $24 billion and expanded to 192 countries, a 240-fold growth in five years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Last year, it had grown to $24 billion and expanded to 192 countries − a growth of 240 times in five years The speed at which companies need to grow and seize market share in the age of disruptive technologies is a matter of life and death for them.

sections.label: AEC, OBOR and AIIB opportunity
sections.summary: The ASEAN Economic Community 2015, China's OBOR initiative and AIIB funding give a fresh opportunity to shape a narrative placing Singapore centrally.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The ASEAN Economic Community 2015 and China's One Belt One Road (OBOR) initiative, together with funding streams from the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB), give us a fresh opportunity to shape a narrative that puts Singapore in the centre of capital flows, international cooperation and development.

sections.label: China capital exports and Singapore hubs
sections.summary: China became a net exporter of capital in 2015, and World Bank and ADB infrastructure hubs and project finance banks are established in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Further, China has become a net exporter of capital in 2015, with non-financial outbound direct investments exceeding inbound FDI.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Already, the World Bank Group's Infrastructure and Development Hub and Page: 66 the Asian Development Bank's (ADB's) Asian Infrastructure Centre of Excellence are established in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: We are a hub for various infrastructure funds and project finance banks, such as Standard Chartered, Sumitomo Mitsui, that have their project finance desks here and can work hand-in-hand with the likes of the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (ICBC) to provide financing options.

sections.label: Rakuten and Double Negative exiting Singapore
sections.summary: Rakuten and Double Negative are exiting Singapore, and a Randstad report showed millennials are less confident about the job market.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Yet, against this backdrop, we also have recent news of much-touted companies in high-growth sectors, such as Rakuten and Double Negative, exiting Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: These are dark clouds for our workers, including our youths and millennials.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: A report by Randstad showed that our millennials are less confident about the job market and fear they may lose their jobs.

sections.label: Future of employment facilitation
sections.summary: The future of employment facilitation must change.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: In essence, the future of employment facilitation must change.

sections.label: Broadening apprenticeship system adoption
sections.summary: The speaker says the apprenticeship system must be broadened so youths in certain industries are better prepared for work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: I now come to the second facet of transforming employment facilitation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: We need to broaden the adoption of the apprenticeship system so that, for certain industries, our youths are much better prepared for work.

sections.label: ICT transformation employment facilitation
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Government to enhance employment facilitation and worker care, and asks how working Singaporeans will maintain income while gaining new competencies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: In ensuring the success of this ICT transformation, I would like to encourage the Government to consider enhancing two key areas: one, stronger employment facilitation; and, two, care for workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: It was announced that the ICT sector will offer 15,000 jobs over the next three years, thereby providing many opportunities for Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: To ramp up our national capabilities quickly, we should fill these jobs not only with new entrants from the Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs), but also from millennials seeking career changes and displaced mid-career information technology (IT) professionals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: How will the Government help working Singaporeans to maintain their income while working towards these new competencies?

sections.label: Foreign work pass holders in ICT
sections.summary: The passage notes one-third of ICT workers are foreign work pass holders and asks how young Singaporeans will not be crowded out of good jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: While the proportion of resident-to-work-pass-holders in the ICT sector is reflective of other sectors in Singapore, we note that one-third of them are foreign work pass holders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: While a Singaporean Core is one that taps on the diversity of skills of that industry's workforce, how can the Government Page: 69 work towards ensuring that young Singaporeans are not crowded out of good jobs?

sections.label: Challenges facing SMEs
sections.summary: Many SMEs face challenges including lack of business opportunities, high financing and business cost, and difficulties retaining talent.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Many SMEs face challenges, such as lack of business opportunities, high financing and business cost, and difficulties with retaining talent.

sections.label: PIC grants and flat productivity
sections.summary: Productivity growth has remained flat despite high PIC grant take-up, with many SMEs using PIC to replace machines and add ICT devices without restructuring work processes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: As highlighted by the Finance Minister, productivity growth has remained flat despite the high take-up rate of PIC grants.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Many SMEs are simply using PIC to replace their old machines and add new ICT devices without restructuring their work processes to improve productivity.

sections.label: De-registered charities in Singapore
sections.summary: The Straits Times reported 97 charities were de-registered between 2010 and 2014 due to difficulties getting staff, volunteers and donations, and there are over 2,000 charities today.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: As reported in The Straits Times on 26 March 2016, 97 charities were de-registered between 2010 and 2014 due to difficulties in getting staff, volunteers and donations.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: To date, there are over 2,000 charities in Singapore.

sections.label: Healthy lifestyle clubs and Budget 2016
sections.summary: The North West CDC set up healthy lifestyle clubs and urges a Healthy Lifestyle Endowment Fund, while Budget 2016 balances reform with counter-cyclical measures.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: At the North West Community Development Council (CDC), we have set up hundreds of healthy lifestyle clubs for our residents.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: In this regard, I urge the Finance Minister to consider setting up a Healthy Lifestyle Endowment Fund to support organisations which champion a healthy lifestyle.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Promoting health among Singaporeans will improve their quality of life, increase their productivity at work and reduce the healthcare expenditure of our country.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: A healthy ageing population will also reduce the financial impact on families and reduce the tax burden for future generations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: It is a Budget that addresses the needs of the business community, especially those in the oil and gas industry and the oil-and-gas related industries – a sector that has seen a sharp decline in business conditions in line with the fall in oil prices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Budget 2016 aims to balance the need to sustain reform with short-term counter-cyclical measures to support slowing growth.

sections.label: Current year PAYE income tax
sections.summary: The speaker suggests relooking at moving to a current year pay-as-you-earn basis of income tax assessment as an automatic economic stabiliser.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: We have focused a lot on the medium to long term and they are very valued measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: But at this point, I would like to suggest that we relook at the option of moving to a current year pay-as-you-earn (PAYE) basis of income tax assessment as an automatic economic stabiliser.

sections.label: Australia and Malaysia tax transition
sections.summary: Australia and Malaysia are successful countries that have transitioned to the current year basis tax system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Successful countries which have successfully transitioned to the current year basis tax system include Australia and Malaysia.

sections.label: More bite for TAFEP
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Government to give more bite to TAFEP to reinforce measures for the medium to long term.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Even as we help to support our people through change in this Budget, I strongly urge the Government to give more bite to the Tripartite Alliance for Fair and Progressive Employment Practices (TAFEP) to reinforce what measures we are doing now for the medium to long term.

sections.label: Lower town centre parking charges
sections.summary: The speaker suggests lowering or making free parking charges at town centres during lunch hour and HDB managing tenant mix.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: One thought that comes to mind or a simple quick way is to lower or make free parking charges at town centres during lunch hour, especially for those which are not located in populous or popular neighbourhoods.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: HDB could also look into actively managing the tenant mix Page: 73 at these centres, so that there are wider and more attractive choices to draw customers.
