sections.label: Recruiting mid-career retrenched people
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Government to recruit more mid-career people and give priority to those who were retrenched.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: They become Singaporean expatriates, a small but growing breed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: So, I urge the Government to look into recruiting more mid-career people and give priority to those who were retrenched.

sections.label: Budget's three main thrusts
sections.summary: The Budget has three thrusts: growing fiscal spending with a prudent Budget, the Industry Transformation Programme, and support for firms and people facing changes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The three main thrusts of this Budget are: one, a growing fiscal spending alongside a prudent Budget; two, the Industry Transformation Programme to create new value and spur growth; and three, to support firms and our people in facing present challenges, including demographic, cyclical and structural changes that are ongoing.

sections.label: Support for Malay/Muslim firms
sections.summary: Malay/Muslim firms can still benefit from previous Budget measures, and are urged to use Industry Transformation Programme and Automation Support Package support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Malay/Muslim firms can still receive benefits from measures introduced during the previous Budget, including wider support through the Transition Support Package.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: But I urge the Malay/Muslim companies to, if possible, make use of the support given through the Industry Transformation Programme and the Automation Support Package to increase their restructuring efforts because the opportunities to compete are growing smaller.

sections.label: Job market and welfare support
sections.summary: Most MENDAKI SENSE jobseekers in 2015 had N/O levels or ITE/diploma qualifications, and the Budget balances economic policies with welfare and income support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: If we look at the situation in the current job market, 40% of those seeking jobs through MENDAKI SENSE in 2015 are those with GCE "N" and "O" level certificates as their highest qualifications.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Another 30% possess either the Institute of Technical Education (ITE) or diploma qualifications.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: If this trend goes on and the spectre of an economic downturn becomes a reality, it is very possible that this will have a cascading effect on the economic status of Malay/Muslim families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: It is hoped that the Adapt and Grow as well as the TechSkills Accelerator initiatives, will help our rank-and-file workers and our PMETs in general, and in the IT sector, to adapt in terms of seeking jobs and upgrading to the necessary skills, as well as work with accredited employers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The 2016 Budget's focus on economic policies is also balanced by welfare assistance and income support for the elderly, low-wage workers and the young, as well as general measures to help households cope with the cost of living.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I hope that the Government's assistance through the First Step Grant can be extended to single mothers so that their children, too, can receive the benefits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: In addition, I welcome the Fresh Start scheme and hope that the conditions stipulated for families to receive the grant will not be too strict.

sections.label: Record retrenchments and PMET layoffs
sections.summary: Last year saw over 15,000 retrenchments and layoffs, 71% of them PMETs, and this round involves structural as well as cyclical forces.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: In fact, last year, we saw a record of more than 15,000 retrenchments and layoffs, and 71% of them were PMETs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: I am expecting things not to get rosier this year; well, at least for the first half of this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: What is so unique this round is that it will not just be cyclical forces alone but also structural.

sections.label: SkillsFuture and Industry Transformation Programme
sections.summary: Workers are no longer immune due to job obsolescence and disruptive technology, and plans were rolled out via SkillsFuture and the Industry Transformation Programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: They are no longer immune because of job obsolescence, disruptive technology, shared economy, crowd sourcing and the Internet of Things.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: I am glad that strategic plans and measures have been rolled out via SkillsFuture last year and the relentless efforts this year to transform our economy through enterprise and innovation via the Industry Transformation Programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: I support the Budget and applaud the Adapt and Grow initiatives announced by Minister Heng.

sections.label: Adapt and Grow for PMEs
sections.summary: The Adapt and Grow initiative should address workers' needs, especially PMEs, by enhancing the Career Support Programme to boost hiring of Singaporean PMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: On the part of the Government, the Adapt and Grow initiative should address our current challenges and the pressing needs of our workers, especially our PMEs, as we row across choppy waters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: First, enhancing the existing Career Support Programme (CSP) to give a boost to hiring our Singaporean PMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: This can be done by widening its outreach, stretching its coverage and deepening its assistance to all PMEs, especially the mature PMEs as well as all PMEs regardless of age who have been retrenched or are unemployed.

sections.label: Heavy hand on recalcitrant companies
sections.summary: Strengthening the Singaporean Core by acting firmly against recalcitrant companies that ignore scrutiny and warnings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Second, strengthening the Singaporean Core by wielding a heavy hand against recalcitrant companies with the ‘"double weak" and which turn a deaf ear to scrutiny and warnings.

sections.label: NTUC Career Activation Programme pilot
sections.summary: NTUC's U PME Centre has piloted the Career Activation Programme for one year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: NTUC's U PME Centre has piloted this for one year and is called the Career Activation Programme.

sections.label: Net Investment Returns Contribution in Budget 2016
sections.summary: Budget 2016 saw a large rise in projected Net Investment Returns Contribution to $14.7 billion, without which the Budget would be in deficit of $11.3 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: One of the things that jumped out in Budget 2016 was the huge increase in the projected Net Investment Returns Contribution (NIRC) to $14.7 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Without NIRC, the 2016 Budget will be in deficit of $11.3 billion.

sections.label: MTI 2016 GDP growth forecast
sections.summary: For 2016, MTI maintained the GDP growth forecast at only 1% to 3%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: For 2016, MTI has maintained the GDP growth forecast at only 1% to 3%.

sections.label: Government future investments and R&D budget
sections.summary: The Government is investing in infrastructure, SkillsFuture, R&D and innovation, with science and technology research budget rising to a record $19 billion over five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: To prepare for the future, the Government is investing more in infrastructure development, including healthcare, public transport and Changi Airport, upgrading Singaporeans through SkillsFuture, pumping more funding into research and development (R&D) and placing a stronger emphasis on technology adoption and innovation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: It was announced in January this year that our Government's science and technology research budget will rise to a record of $19 billion in the next five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: This works out to be roughly $4 billion each year, which is around 1% of our GDP, comparable to the US' spending on R&D.

sections.label: Extending Work Permit levy deferment
sections.summary: The speaker appreciates deferring levy increases for marine and process sectors and maintaining manufacturing levies, but wants these extended to services and construction Work Permit holders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: While I appreciate the deferment of levy increases for Work Permit holders in the marine and process sectors for one year, as well as maintaining the manufacturing Work Permit levies for another year, I feel that these should be extended to the services and construction Work Permit holders as well.

sections.label: Deferring levy increases, foreign worker quotas
sections.summary: Calls for deferring levy increases by one year and for the Ministry to work with TACs on benchmarks and controlling quota or levy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: In this uncertain business climate and with Page: 81 near-term cyclical weaknesses, we ought to act proactively to support these businesses by deferring the levy increases by one year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: On a broader front, would the Ministry work with Trade Associations and Chambers (TACs) to look into setting benchmarks and controlling either the quota or the levy instead of both simultaneously?

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: This will give businesses more flexibility to drive their business and to have a better mix in the number and type of foreign workers they can employ.

sections.label: Slowdown cyclical and structural
sections.summary: Concludes that the current slowdown is both cyclical and, more fundamentally, structural.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: My conclusion is that the current slowdown is both cyclical and more fundamentally, structural.

sections.label: SkillsFuture funding and future jobs
sections.summary: States that over $1 billion was committed to SkillsFuture last year, with this year's focus on creating jobs of the future.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Last year, we embarked on SkillsFuture and we committed more than $1 billion to upgrade the skills of our workers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: We, in NTUC and the People's Association and many service providers, are ramping up relevant courses to meet the needs of our workers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: So, yes, we have committed $1 billion as a first tranche to try and get ourselves up to speed with the skills of the future.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: This year, the focus is on trying to create jobs of the future.

sections.label: Winding down scheme dependence
sections.summary: Says success is marked by slowly but surely winding down the proportion of workers dependent on such schemes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Our mark of success is that in time to come, we are able to slowly, but surely, wind down the proportion of workers who are dependent on such schemes.

sections.label: Tackling structural unemployment
sections.summary: States that the first matter concerns efforts to tackle possible structural unemployment.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: The first has to do with our effort to tackle possible structural unemployment.

sections.label: NTUC tripartite partnership actions
sections.summary: States that NTUC and the Labour Movement can do three things much better in partnership with tripartite partners.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: From NTUC and the Labour Movement's perspective, we can do three things much better in partnership with the tripartite partners.

sections.label: NTUC WDA details later
sections.summary: NTUC and WDA will announce more details later in the year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: NTUC, together with WDA, will announce more details later in the year.

sections.label: SkillsFuture credit account balance
sections.summary: Today they all have $500 in their SkillsFuture credit account.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Today, they all have $500 in their SkillsFuture credit account.

sections.label: Labour Movement retirement adequacy concern
sections.summary: The Labour Movement's second big concern is ensuring retirement adequacy.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: The second big concern that the Labour Movement has is ensuring retirement adequacy.

sections.label: Re-examining fixed retirement age
sections.summary: Many people want to work longer, so ways to re-examine the fixed retirement age should be found.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Many of our people want to work longer and we should find ways to re-examine this concept of a fixed retirement age to allow Singaporeans with the experience and capabilities to contribute as long as where they want.

sections.label: Retirement adequacy and CPF base pay
sections.summary: The challenge is not just whether older workers get 20% past 60 or 65, as unscrupulous employers may lower base pay.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Our challenge, when we come to speak about retirement adequacy, is not just talking about whether the older workers should get 20% when they are past the age of 60 or 65.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: This is because, if the employers are unscrupulous, they will tell you that, "I can give you back your 20% CPF if I lower your base pay".

sections.label: Challenging construction retail F&B sectors
sections.summary: Construction, retail and food and beverage are three particularly challenging sectors requiring greater attention to lift national productivity.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: In terms of sectors, there are three sectors that are particularly challenging and require us to pay much greater attention to if we are to lift the overall productivity number of our country.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: They are construction, retail and food and beverage (F&B) sectors.

sections.label: Productivity and upfront design
sections.summary: The passage calls for unity in re-examining mindsets and methods, arguing jobs cannot be uplifted without designing security upfront.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: But if we are truly serious about raising our productivity across all sectors, let us all unite together to re-examine our mindsets and methods.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: There is no way that we can design a higher paying job for the security guard if the building has not been designed for security right from the onset.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: As Churchill would have said, "Once we design a building in three months, the building will take the next 30 years to design us"; and it will design our jobs as well.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: If we do not design security upfront, there is no way that we can uplift the productivity of our workers downstream.

sections.label: Singapore Core workforce
sections.summary: It states belief in working with companies to build a strong Singapore Core, which does not mean an all-Singaporean workforce.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: We believe in urging and working with all companies to build a strong Singapore Core.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: But that Singapore Core does not mean that it is an all-Singaporean workforce.

sections.label: Singaporeans in top oil jobs
sections.summary: It states that Singaporeans today hold the country's top jobs at Exxon Mobile and Shell.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Today, the persons holding the country's top jobs in Exxon Mobile and Shell are Singaporeans.

sections.label: SMEs' highs, less, lack, difficulties
sections.summary: It lists SMEs' three highs, three less, three lacks and three difficulties.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: First, SMEs face three "highs" – high rental, high wages and high levy.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: They also have three "less" – less business, less profit and less workers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: They feel that there is a "lack" in three areas – the bosses lack power, the workers lack motivation and landlords lack empathy.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: And they face three "difficulties" – difficulty in doing business, difficulty in getting workers and difficulty in securing a shop space.

sections.label: NTUC training for SME HR
sections.summary: It states NTUC will launch training programmes to help SMEs strengthen human resource management.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: In this regard, NTUC will launch training programmes to help our SMEs strengthen human resource management.

sections.label: NTUC working with SME bosses
sections.summary: It states NTUC will continue working with SME bosses and others, as the next step requires people and businesses together.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Moving forward, NTUC will continue to work with SME bosses and other organisations because we believe that the Government has taken the first step.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: The next step requires both people and businesses to work together.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: By doing so, we will be able to overcome both the current cyclical issues and long-term structural challenges.

sections.label: Automation Support Package commended
sections.summary: The speaker commends the $400 million Automation Support Package as a powerful tool.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
sentences.text: First, I must commend that the $400 million Automation Support Package (ASP) is a powerful tool.

sections.label: National Robotics Programme comment
sections.summary: The speaker comments on the $450 million National Robotics Programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
sentences.text: Next, let me comment on the $450 million National Robotics Programme.

sections.label: Global robot spending growth
sections.summary: Global spending on robots is expected to quadruple to $67 billion by 2025, creating 3.5 million new jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
sentences.text: In fact, global spending on robots is expected to quadruple to $67 billion by 2025, creating some 3.5 million new jobs in the process.

sections.label: National Research Fund top-up
sections.summary: Minister Heng announced the Ministry would provide a $1.5 billion top-up to the National Research Fund this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
sentences.text: Minister Heng announced earlier that the Ministry would provide a $1.5 billion top-up to the National Research Fund this year.

sections.label: R&D economic spin-offs 2013
sections.summary: The 2013 national R&D survey attributed $23.8 billion in economic spin-offs to R&D.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
sentences.text: According to the 2013 national R&D survey, economic spin-offs attributed to R&D was $23.8 billion.

sections.label: R&D funding and four sectors
sections.summary: Local enterprises and SMEs hope for more R&D funding, and two changes would help harness four sectors' spin-offs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
sentences.text: Large local enterprises and SMEs especially, are hoping that more R&D funding can be directed to them for better local value capture and IP-retentions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
sentences.text: They are the Health and Biomedical Sciences sector, the Advanced Manufacturing and Engineering sector, the Urban Solutions and Sustainability sector and the Services and Digital Economy sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
sentences.text: To fully harness the economic spin-offs of these four sectors, two changes would be helpful: one, Ministries and their agencies to take on industry-development roles; and two, agencies outside MTI be given the investment promotion tools to undertake economic development under the whole-of-Government approach.

sections.label: LEAD programme and TACs
sections.summary: The Ministry is enhancing the LEAD programme to strengthen TACs, as empowering Ministries and agencies is a more effective way for industry development.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
sentences.text: Given the inter-disciplinary nature of problems in urban solutions, a more effective way for industry development for this new vertical would be to empower Ministries and agencies involved to take on industry development roles, by giving them the necessary tools to do so.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
sentences.text: In this regard, I am pleased to note that the Ministry is enhancing the LEAD programme to strengthen our TACs so that they can do more for their members.

sections.label: SFIC and other TACs
sections.summary: SFIC is well-organised and well-run, but not every TAC is, and the enhanced LEAD+ programme is hoped to help more TACs professionalise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
sentences.text: While SFIC is well-organised and well-run, the same cannot be said of every TAC.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
sentences.text: I hope the enhanced LEAD+ programme will help many more TACs to professionalise and level up.

sections.label: China's market and economy
sections.summary: China is the world's largest market for smart phones and e-commerce, has 100 cities over a million people, and is expected to overtake America as largest economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
sentences.text: It is common knowledge by now that China is the world's largest market for smart phones and e-commerce and mobile, or m-commerce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
sentences.text: It has 100 cities with more than a million people, and Shanghai alone is 4.2 times the size of Singapore in population and talent terms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
sentences.text: China's outward investments started to outstrip its inward investments last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
sentences.text: Economists expect China to overtake America somewhere between 2020 and 2030 to be the world's largest economy.

sections.label: Singapore science, R&D, Mandarin
sections.summary: Without adequate science and technology capability there was no basis for the seminar, so Singapore must redouble R&D efforts and pay attention to Mandarin and regional languages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
sentences.text: But the title also meant that if Singapore Page: 93 did not have adequate science and technology capability, there was no basis for this seminar.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
sentences.text: We must redouble our efforts in R&D, applying our R&D resources to industries, get our young people interested in science and technology and pay serious attention to the learning of Mandarin and regional languages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
sentences.text: If we stagnate, if we close our doors to foreign talents and new ideas, the Singapore Core will be weakened and Singapore will diminish.

sections.label: Budget 2016 help for SMEs
sections.summary: A good part of Budget 2016 is geared towards targeted help for viable local businesses, including SMEs, through the Loan Assistance scheme and Industry Transformation Programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: It is, therefore, reassuring that a good part of Budget 2016 has been geared towards extending more targeted help to viable local businesses to help them weather these toughening conditions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I refer particularly to those measures targeted towards our SMEs, such as the Loan Assistance scheme and the Industry Transformation Programme.

sections.label: Businesses with flawed models
sections.summary: Businesses with fundamental flaws in their business models, such as over-reliance on cheap labour or Government subsidies, should be allowed to die a natural death.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Businesses with fundamental flaws in their business models, for example, those that are over-reliant on cheap labour or Government subsidies, should be allowed to die a natural death.

sections.label: Co-hawking spaces and legal templates
sections.summary: Suggests mall co-hawking spaces for startup F&B businesses and SPRING Singapore standard templates or low-cost legal firms for startups.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Would it be possible, for example, to collaborate with mall operators to offer "co-hawking" spaces, providing startup F&B businesses access to high traffic at affordable rent with flexible lease terms to test out their concepts for six months before graduating to permanent locations if they prove successful?

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Currently, a law firm can easily quote $10,000 to $15,000 or more for a shareholders' agreement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Perhaps SPRING Singapore could consider providing standard templates for startups to use or to seek to partner startup-focused low-cost legal firms.

sections.label: Mr Chua's late salary payments
sections.summary: Mr Chua liquidated holdings and went into debt, could not pay levies and salaries in time, and was charged by MOM for 16 counts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: As a result, Mr Chua had had to liquidate all his personal holdings and to go into debt to try to pay his workers' levies and salaries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: However, due to the illiquid nature of his assets, he was ultimately unable to make all the necessary payments in time, and although his workers' levies and salaries have largely been paid, and all affected foreign workers have been successfully repatriated, Mr Chua was charged by MOM in Court for 16 counts of contravention of the Employment Act for the late salary payments.

sections.label: Schemes of arrangement for SMEs
sections.summary: Schemes of arrangement had a 77.1% success rate in 48 cases from 2002 to 2009 but are rarely used by SMEs due to cost and negotiation delays.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Schemes of arrangement appear to be the most popular corporate rescue regime and a study from 2002 to 2009 by the Insolvency and Public Trustee's Office showed a 77.1% success rate out of 48 cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Currently, they are rarely used by SMEs as they are prohibitively expensive to set up, with all parties engaging lawyers to negotiate their positions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Negotiations can also drag on as 75% of each class of creditors needs to agree.

sections.label: Super priority financing plans
sections.summary: There are plans to permit super priority financing to help businesses attract funds to restructure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Currently, there are plans to permit "super priority financing" to help these businesses attract funds to restructure their businesses.

sections.label: Supporting risk takers
sections.summary: Risk takers who aim high but fall need support to rise again, and the global economy is anticipated to slow this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: So, we need to ensure that risk takers who aim high but fall are provided the necessary support to enable them to rise again.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: It is anticipated that the global economy will slow this year.

sections.label: Singapore's economic restructuring
sections.summary: Singapore faces global headwinds and will also go through its own economic restructuring.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Singapore, apart from facing these global headwinds, will also be going through its own economic restructuring.

sections.label: Continued support and SEC extension
sections.summary: Measures continuing include Transition Support Package support and extension of the Senior Employment Credit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Page: 97 There are also a number of measures that are going to continue and these include continued support from the Transition Support Package, as well as the extension of the Senior Employment Credit (SEC).

sections.label: Modest Budget surplus
sections.summary: Despite being an expansionary Budget, there is still going to be a modest Budget surplus overall.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: On a related note, although this is an expansionary Budget, I am heartened that, overall, there is still going to be a modest Budget surplus.

sections.label: Budget schemes within balanced Budget
sections.summary: GST Vouchers, Silver Support, S&CC rebates, CDA grants and KidSTART fall within this category and are welcomed as provided within a balanced Budget.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The Budget schemes including GST Vouchers, Silver Support, service and conservancy changes (S&CC) rebates and support for children through Children Development Account (CDA) grants and KidSTART, all fall within this category and, as they are all being provided within the context of a balanced Budget, they are to be welcomed.

sections.label: Indian families and preschool
sections.summary: About 17% of Indian families had not sent their children to preschool, which may lead to difficulties in primary school.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: About 17% of Indian families had not sent their children to preschool, and this may lead to more difficulties for them once they start primary school as they will not have had the same head start as their peers.

sections.label: First Step Grant and CDA matching
sections.summary: The First Step Grant provides $3,000 into the child's CDA account, and parents continue to enjoy dollar-for-dollar matching.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: First, the First Step Grant provides $3,000 into the child's CDA account.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Additionally, parents will also continue to enjoy dollar-for-dollar matching for amounts put into the CDA grant.

sections.label: KidSTART help for low-income families
sections.summary: KidSTART will provide additional help for low-income families for the first six years of their lives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Additionally, the KidSTART scheme will provide additional help for low-income families for the first six years of their lives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The Minister mentioned that this is in recognition of the importance of the early years of education and to ensure that children from poorer backgrounds do not miss out on this.

sections.label: Singapore engines of growth
sections.summary: Singapore has four main engines of growth since 1819, with manufacturing developed as the second after Independence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Page: 99 From 1819, when Stamford Raffles first set foot on our shores until today, Singapore can be said to have four main engines of growth.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: After Independence, we developed manufacturing as our second engine of growth.

sections.label: Regional financial centre growth
sections.summary: The third engine of growth was developing Singapore as a regional financial and wealth management centre.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Our third engine of growth was the development of Singapore as a regional financial and wealth management centre.

sections.label: Tourism as fourth engine
sections.summary: Revitalising Marina Bay and opening two integrated resorts boosted tourism, the fourth engine of growth.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: With the revitalisation of the Marina Bay area and the opening of our two integrated resorts, we gave a further boost to tourism, our fourth engine of growth.

sections.label: Budget 2016 industry transformation
sections.summary: Budget 2016 seeks to transform industries to strengthen expertise and drive growth through innovation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Budget 2016 seeks to transform our industries to strengthen our expertise and drive growth through innovation.

sections.label: Heng Swee Keat measures
sections.summary: Minister for Finance Heng Swee Keat unveiled measures including new SME schemes and increased public spending to soften the blow.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: In response, Minister for Finance Heng Swee Keat has unveiled a raft of measures which the Government will be undertaking to soften the blow, from introducing new schemes for SMEs to increasing public spending.

sections.label: Productivity growth target shortfall
sections.summary: The 2010 target was 2% to 3% annual productivity growth over 10 years, but growth was 0.3% over 2009 and 2014.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: The productivity growth target for the economy, as outlined by the Economic Strategies Committee in 2010, was 2% to 3% a year over 10 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: If we exclude the post-financial crisis rebound in 2010, productivity growth came in at a compounded annual growth rate of 0.3% over 2009 and 2014.

sections.label: Cash payout claims 2011-2015
sections.summary: About 71,000 cash payout claims amounting to $3.6 billion were made between 2011 and 2015.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Since then, about 71,000 cash payout claims amounting to $3.6 billion were made between 2011 and 2015.

sections.label: SEC fund top-up
sections.summary: The SEC fund will be topped up by $1.1 billion this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: The SEC fund will be topped up by $1.1 billion this year.

sections.label: Sankaran on Government subsidies
sections.summary: Mr Sankaran said Government subsidies, if not implemented appropriately, could hide SME inefficiency and become a crutch.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Mr Sankaran, Vice Chairman of Makino Asia Group Companies, also shared with me that Government subsidies, if not implemented appropriately, could hide SME's inefficiency and, at times become a crutch rather than helping them to run.

sections.label: Hiring and seconding public officers
sections.summary: The Civil Service could hire private sector executives, and seconding public officers to TACs and SMEs is suggested.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: The Civil Service could hire promising executives from the private sector to supplement its policy team.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: For instance, venture capitalist and entrepreneur, Dr Finian Tan, joined the Administrative Service for a few years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: However, the practice of recruiting mid-career executives into the Public Service appears to have stopped.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: The initiative to second up to 20 public officers to TACs, to help Government agencies to better understand enterprises' needs and to support TACs in developing their capabilities and strengthening their processes and services, is a good first step.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: In deepening private sector understanding, the Government may also want to consider seconding public officers to promising SMEs.

sections.label: World Economic Forum jobs report
sections.summary: The 2016 World Economic Forum report indicates about seven million jobs could be lost over five years, partly offset by two million new jobs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The 2016 World Economic Forum report on "The Future of Jobs" indicates that over the next five years, about seven million jobs could be lost through redundancy, automation or disintermediation, meaning the removal of the middleman in business processes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: This loss is predicted to be only partially offset by about two million new jobs and mostly in the more specialised families such as Computer Engineering.

sections.label: SMEs in Singapore
sections.summary: SMEs make up 99% of enterprises in Singapore and contribute more than 50% of GDP.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: First up, is our SMEs which make up 99% of enterprises in Singapore and contributing more than 50% of our gross domestic product (GDP).

sections.label: Layoffs hit skilled middle-aged
sections.summary: A March 2016 Straits Times article reported highly skilled, middle-aged employees were hardest hit by layoffs, seen as too costly and too old.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: A The Straits Times article in March 2016 reported that the group that was hardest hit by layoffs last year was our highly skilled and middle-aged employees who were seen by firms as too costly for their previous firms to retain and supposedly too old for prospective employees to hire.

sections.label: SMEs, PMETs, lower-skilled at risk
sections.summary: SMEs, PMETs and lower-skilled Singaporeans are at risk of being left behind.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Our SMEs, PMETs and lower-skilled Singaporeans are at risk of being left behind.

sections.label: Profiling by three As
sections.summary: The passage proposes profiling SMEs, PMETs, lower-skilled workers and VWOs by ability, attitude and altitude.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Profile the SMEs, PMETs, the lower-skilled workers and even the volunteer welfare organisations (VWOs) by three "A"s: one, the ability – current and potential ability, knowledge, skills and tools; two, their attitude – their willingness to update, upgrade; and three, their altitude – the vision, the ability to rise above themselves in the industry in the current terrain.

sections.label: Linking resources and removing barriers
sections.summary: The passage calls for linking them to R&D, investors and mentors, removing barriers, and creating more clusters and mini Innovative Parks.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Link them up with research and development (R&D) resources, angel investors or even global mentors; remove the barriers to performance which are within Government's circle of influence; create more Block 71 clusters to reduce the cost of business in rental and other shared corporate services such as in finance, legal and audit; develop even more mini Innovative Parks beyond the mega Jurong Innovation Park.

sections.label: SkillsFuture credit as nudge
sections.summary: The $500 SkillsFuture credit is welcome but serves as a nudge at best and does not guarantee lifelong learning.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Whilst the $500 SkillsFuture credit to every Singaporean is a great welcome, it serves as a nudge at best, and is no guarantee that it will lead to an innate desire to learn or to learn lifelong.

sections.label: Future-Readiness Self-Assessment Toolkit courses
sections.summary: The passage proposes freely accessible Future-Readiness Self-Assessment Toolkit and bite-sized tasters at neighbourhood sites or online, listing eight courses.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Fourth, we must make pervasive, freely accessible Future-Readiness Self-Assessment Toolkit and bite-sized tasters at convenient neighbourhood sites, the community centres or online, with courses such as: (a) Using video and voice applications such as Skype; (b) Taking great digital photos; (c) Setting up online stores from scratch; (d) Construct our own website; (e) Learn to Code; (f) Create simple Apps on the smartphone; (g) Make objects through customised 3-D printing; (h) Write for the Internet.

sections.label: Budget theme Partnership for the Future
sections.summary: The Budget theme is called "Partnership for the Future", described as typical of Minister Heng Swee Keat's style to listen and engage the ground.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Typical of Minister Heng Swee Keat's style to listen and engage the ground, the theme of the Budget is termed "Partnership for the Future".

sections.label: Trade associations and industry transformation
sections.summary: The passage suggests co-shared targets, space for SMEs, senior public officers, and paid global industry advisors for industry panels comprising trade associations and other players.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Trade associations, like other organisations, comprise of us mortals who may not all share the same vision or agree on the same tactics, and may be distracted by politics and personalities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: It would be useful, as we pour more resources into industry-led transformations, to also set some targets that are co-shared by all the partners.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: We must allow space for SMEs with the ability, attitude and altitude to charter their paths – without insisting that they must toe the line of their industry associations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Public officers who are supposed to be sent to assist the industries should preferably be senior enough to impact policy making.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: We should invite or even pay for successful global industry leaders to sit as advisors to industry panels which comprise the trade associations and the other member players.

sections.label: BIPS donations to VWOs
sections.summary: The passage states that BIPS donations should not be limited to only $50,000 for each VWO.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Do not limit the BIPS donations to only $50,000 for each VWO.

sections.label: Singaporeans expect terrorist attack
sections.summary: A Sunday Times poll found three in four Singaporeans believe an attack is only a matter of time, echoing the Minister for Home Affairs and Law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In a recent poll done by The Sunday Times, it was found that three in four Singaporeans believe that it is only a matter of time before Singapore faces a terrorist attack.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: This echoes the sentiments of our Minister for Home Affairs and Law, who also acknowledged that it is, "no longer a question of whether an attack will take place but when an attack is going to take place in Singapore".

sections.label: Internal security against terrorism
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Government has considered areas needing more work to beef up internal security and what is being done to plug gaps.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In light of this, has the Government considered whether there are areas where more needs to be done to beef up our internal security to deal with the threat of terrorism?

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: What is being done to plug any gaps in our internal security framework?

sections.label: Flexible work arrangements increase
sections.summary: The Minister for Manpower shared that employers providing at least one form of FWA rose from 28% in 2008 to 47% in 2014.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In January this year, the Minister for Manpower shared that the proportion of employers providing at least one form of FWA for their employees has steadily increased from 28% in 2008 to 47% in 2014.

sections.label: Flexi-work or no-pay leave option
sections.summary: The speaker proposes working mothers be given the option of eight weeks of flexi-work or eight weeks of no-pay leave.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In fact, I believe that the Government should consider taking it one step further.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I am proposing that working mothers be given the option to choose between either taking an additional eight weeks of flexi-work or an additional eight weeks of no-pay leave.

sections.label: Legislating leave option for mothers
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Government would consider legislating an option for working mothers to choose eight weeks of unpaid leave or eight weeks of FWAs after maternity leave.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In light of this, would the Government consider legislating this option for working mothers to choose between either having eight weeks of unpaid leave or having eight weeks of FWAs after the current 16 weeks of maternity leave?

sections.label: Removing ABSDs for Singaporean buyers
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Government would consider gradually removing ABSDs for Singaporean buyers while retaining TDSR for Singaporeans and ABSDs for foreigners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: As such, would the Government consider the gradual and calibrated approach of removing ABSDs for Singaporean buyers, while still retaining the TDSR for Singaporeans and retaining the ABSDs for foreigners?

sections.label: Adapting Australian model in Singapore
sections.summary: The speaker suggests the Government consider adapting the Australian model in Singapore if it fears removing property cooling measures may cause the market to surge.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: If the Government is concerned that removing the existing property cooling measures may cause the market to surge upward exponentially, perhaps the Government would also consider adapting the Australian model in Singapore, which I have raised in this House before.

sections.label: Publicising adoption to pregnant women
sections.summary: The speaker believes adoption could be publicised more widely and pregnant women given more information about adoption as a voluntary alternative.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Many of these women may not be aware of, or might not have thought about, the option of adoption.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I believe that the option of adoption could be publicised more widely, and greater efforts can be made to provide pregnant women with information about the wonderful and voluntary alternative of adoption.

sections.label: Promoting adoption as abortion alternative
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Government would consider promoting adoption as a voluntary alternative for a mother thinking of abortion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I strongly believe that if adoption is more widely publicised as a comforting, loving, nurturing and voluntary alternative, there will be a reduced number of abortions in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Therefore, would the Government consider promoting adoption as a voluntary alternative for a mother who is thinking of abortion?

sections.label: Adoption choice and Budget balance
sections.summary: The passage states adoption is a voluntary choice for a pregnant mother and that this year's Budget balances economy-boosting initiatives with social safety net measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: After all, the choice of an adoption is a voluntary choice that a pregnant mother has to make, and we must do all that we can to support her as she makes an informed choice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: This year's Budget strikes a good balance between initiatives that boost the economy, like the introduction of the SME Working Capital Loan scheme and the Automation Support Package, and also includes measures to strengthen our social safety nets like the enhancements to the Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) scheme and the implementation of the Silver Support Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: All of these initiatives require prudent fiscal planning and a healthy Budget.

sections.label: Heng Swee Keat Budget aims
sections.summary: Finance Minister Heng Swee Keat has put forward a Budget seeking to address near-term cyclical weaknesses and guard against medium-term structural challenges.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: (In English): Finance Minister Heng Swee Keat has put forward a Budget which seeks to address near-term cyclical weaknesses and guard against medium-term structural challenges.

sections.label: Economic transformation means survival
sections.summary: The passage focuses on the Minister's Budget speech acknowledgment that economic transformation is not a choice but a means for survival.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But I would like to focus on the acknowledgment that the Minister has made in his Budget speech.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: He acknowledged that our economic transformation is not a choice, but a means for our survival.

sections.label: Foo Mee Har on deficits
sections.summary: The passage states that Ms Foo Mee Har drew attention to consecutive deficits experienced in the past four financial years.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Yesterday, the hon Member Ms Foo Mee Har rightly drew our attention to the consecutive deficits we have experienced in the past four financial years.

sections.label: Rockefeller Foundation resilient cities recognition
sections.summary: Singapore was recognised by the Rockefeller Foundation in New York as one of 100 resilient cities, an initiative supporting a view of resilience including shocks and stresses.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: On a serious note, Singapore has been recognised as only one of 100 resilient cities throughout the world.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This recognition was by the Rockefeller Foundation in New York.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This initiative of having 100 resilient cities supports the adoption and incorporation of a view of resilience that includes not just the ability to respond to the usual shocks – earthquakes, fires, floods and so on – but also the stresses that may weaken the fabric of a city on a daily or cyclical basis.

sections.label: Building new facilities beyond
sections.summary: The passage states that as new facilities like the Outward Bound Singapore campus at Coney Island are built, which the speaker supports, we have to look beyond.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The first point would be, as we build new facilities, for example, the Outward Bound Singapore (OBS) campus at Coney Island – which I support – I think we have to look beyond.

sections.label: SkillsFuture, Adapt and Grow, Jurong Innovation District
sections.summary: The SkillsFuture programme and Adapt and Grow initiative are means to this, and the Jurong Innovation District is commended as a space for entrepreneurs, researchers and students.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The SkillsFuture programme is one means to do this, as is the Adapt and Grow initiative.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I commend the Jurong Innovation District which the Minister had suggested as a "space for entrepreneurs, researchers and students to design, prototype, and test-bed their new ideas".

sections.label: Grasp of ethics and intellectual property
sections.summary: They should grasp corporate ethics and responsibility, intellectual property rights and patents, and receive action-oriented tutelage from experts, businessmen and technocrat entrepreneurs.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Significantly, they should be able to have a grasp of, among other things, corporate ethics and corporate responsibility; the value and basics of intellectual property rights and patents; and, as many of us in this House have agreed in the past couple of days, proper action-oriented tutelage from experts, other businessmen and technocrat entrepreneurs who can guide them.

sections.label: More action-oriented research projects
sections.summary: The change needed in the education process is for more action-oriented research projects, not just writing but doing.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The change we need to usher in this education process is for more action-oriented research projects, not just writing but doing.

sections.label: University enterprise and innovation hubs
sections.summary: All Singapore universities have enterprise and innovation hubs or laboratories for companies and organisations to collaborate with technology experts and students in industry projects.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: All the universities in Singapore have enterprise and innovation hubs or laboratories for companies and organisations to collaborate with technology experts and students in industry projects.

sections.label: SG Innovate and Young Outstanding Singaporeans
sections.summary: Best ideas are housed, developed and fertilised there, a role SG Innovate could play, and the Young Outstanding Singaporeans awarded over 40 years should perhaps be looked at.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The best ideas are housed, developed and fertilised there.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: That could be a role that SG Innovate plays − to inculcate, develop and hot-house some of the best ideas from all universities.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Closer to home, I would also add that perhaps we should look at the Young Outstanding Singaporeans who have been awarded over the years for the past 40 years.

sections.label: SG Innovate as linking node
sections.summary: SG Innovate will hopefully be the node to link thought leaders and innovators and liaise with existing professional academies, businesses and universities.

sentences.speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: SG Innovate will be that node, hopefully, to link thought leaders, innovators and liaise with our existing professional academies, businesses and universities.

sections.label: Expansionary fiscal policy spending
sections.summary: The speaker notes time has run out and welcomes the Government's expansionary fiscal policy with 7.3% higher total spending than last year.

sentences.speaker: Mdm Speaker
sentences.text: Asst Prof, you have run out of time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I am glad that the Government has decided to opt for an expansionary fiscal policy this year with 7.3% higher total spending over last year.

sections.label: Workfare Income Supplement changes
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes raising the WIS income ceiling from $1,900 to $2,000, monthly WIS payments, and one-month work qualification.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   I welcome the move by the Government to raise the income ceiling of the Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) from $1,900 to $2,000, benefiting about 460,000 Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In addition, the Government will also start paying WIS on a monthly basis instead of quarterly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Another welcome measure is that workers now only need to work for one month to qualify.

sections.label: Workfare Training Support for disabled
sections.summary: The speaker supports measures making persons with disabilities above 13 years old eligible for the Workfare Training Support Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: It is like "sending charcoal in a snowy day".

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I also support the measures to enable persons with disabilities who is above 13 years old to be eligible for the Workfare Training Support (WTS) Scheme.

sections.label: Older PMETs re-employability concerns
sections.summary: The speaker is concerned about re-employability of middle and older PMETs, who are vulnerable in downturns and targeted in cost-cutting restructuring.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The middle and older PMETs are particularly hard hit, and this is a group usually with mortgages to service and still supporting children in school and elderly parents – the typical sandwiched class.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I am deeply concerned with the re-employability of these middle aged or older PMETs as they tend to be vulnerable in an economic downturn, becoming the easy choice of the company's cost-cutting restructuring measures rather than exhausting other alternatives, such as collective wage freeze and adjustment.

sections.label: Career Support Programme funding
sections.summary: The speaker suggests allocating more funds to the Career Support Programme, which offers mature PMETs mid-level jobs with wage support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Perhaps, we should allocate more funds to the Career Support Programme (CSP) which offers more opportunities to mature Singaporean PMETs for mid-level and above jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The CSP has a wage support component and makes it attractive for employers to hire such individuals in any job that pays a gross salary of at least $4,000 a month.

sections.label: Property loan tenure review
sections.summary: The speaker suggests reviewing long-term commitments like property prices and reducing property loan tenure to not more than 20 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: This may mean it warrants a further review of our long-term commitment in life, such as HDB and private property prices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: It may be prudent to reduce the property loan tenure to not more than 20 years in meeting shorter skill life with the advent of technological advancement and stiff market competition.

sections.label: Subsidies for centre workers
sections.summary: The Government may consider letting workers claim subsidies that infant or childcare centres would have claimed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: As a token of recognition for their contribution, the Government may wish to consider allowing them to claim the subsidies which would have been claimed by infant or childcare centres.

sections.label: Silver Support for retirees
sections.summary: The Silver Support Scheme starting in July will supplement this group's retirement income alongside MediShield Life and the Pioneer Generation Package.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For this group, the Silver Support Scheme that will begin in July will serve as a good supplement to their retirement income in addition to the existing support schemes, such as MediShield Life and Pioneer Generation Package.

sections.label: WDA Professional Conversion Programme
sections.summary: WDA's Professional Conversion Programme helps jobseekers re-skill for new jobs, and more can be done to strengthen it through stakeholder collaboration.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Workforce Development Agency's (WDA) Professional Conversion Programme (PCP), which helps jobseekers re-skill themselves to take on new jobs has helped many to switch career pathways.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For example, a 58-year-old union member, who was a Senior Clinic Supervisor took up a nursing diploma course but was only given training allowance of $1,000.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: More can be done to strengthen the PCP by making sure that there is close collaboration amongst all the stakeholders.

sections.label: Mentors and programme selection
sections.summary: Participants can be paired with mentors, and selection must consider an individual's capability and aptitude to keep drop-out rates low.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: They can also be paired with mentors to share insights before, during and after the programme.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Also, to ensure that drop-out rates are low, the selection process of such programmes must take into consideration an individual's capability and aptitude levels.

sections.label: Topping up SkillsFuture Credit
sections.summary: The Government and employers are encouraged to top up the individual's SkillsFuture Credit account to support learning new skills.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Perhaps, to better support the workers in their endeavour to learn new skill, both the Government and employers too, are encouraged to top up the individual's SkillsFuture Credit account.

sections.label: SME workers largely Singaporeans
sections.summary: Workers working in SMEs are largely Singaporeans, which is described as alarming.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: What is alarming is, workers working in SMEs are largely Singaporeans.

sections.label: Safety net for middle-income earners
sections.summary: Calls for a safety net for middle-income earners in dire times and more help between jobs, especially if job search exceeds six months to a year.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: On middle-income earners who are in vulnerable situations, there must be some safety net in dire times should our economy become more sluggish.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: More needs to be done to assist them in between jobs, especially if the job search takes more than six months to a year, or even more.

sections.label: No tax rebate for middle-income earners
sections.summary: Asks why there is no tax rebate for middle-income earners this year, noting a 48% increase from last year's NIRC of $9.9 billion and a $3.4 billion surplus.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Why is there no tax rebate for the middle-income earners this year?

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This is the question that ponders in the mind of the sandwich class as they strongly believe that with the tax rebate, such workers can then have something for their savings and help in their family financial chaos.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This is a substantial increase of about 48% from the NIRC of $9.9 billion at the Government's disposal last year and has given this Government more leeway and flexibility to implement its plans, with the $3.4 billion surplus as well.

sections.label: Budget expenditure and Silver Support
sections.summary: States this year's Budget total expenditure is $73 billion, and the $330 million Silver Support Package will rise in coming years due to the demographic profile.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The total expenditure for this year's Budget comes up to $73 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The $330 million expended on the Silver Support Package will rise in the years to come because of our demographic profile.

sections.label: Workfare payout for 50-year-old employee
sections.summary: States a 50-year-old employee earning $1,800 on Workfare gets an additional $9 cash and $13 CPF monthly, paid quarterly, subject to months employed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Currently, a 50-year-old employee earning $1,800 on Workfare gets an additional $9 in cash and $13 in CPF contributions every month, with the amount payable every quarter, subject to the number of months he or she remains employed.

sections.label: Productivity and Innovation Credit scheme outcomes
sections.summary: Suggests the Government set out how much the PIC scheme improved productivity or spurred innovation, as this year's Budget heralds reduced PIC payouts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For example, it would be helpful for the Government to set out how much the Productivity and Innovation Credit scheme (PIC) has actually improved productivity numbers or even spurred innovation, even as this year's Budget heralds a reduction of PIC payouts going forward.

sections.label: Industry Transformation Programme and productivity differentiation
sections.summary: Suggests considering how companies raising productivity, skills, innovation and internationalisation can benefit more from taxpayer dollars, possibly via a higher corporate income tax rebate cap than $20,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Moving forward, and specifically on the Budget's announcement of the $4.5 billion Industry Transformation Programme with more than 20 sectors earmarked for development, it would be worthwhile to consider how companies and sectors that do the most to raise productivity, improve skills and innovation as well as promoting internationalisation can benefit more from taxpayer dollars than those who do not.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: One way to effect this differentiation is to consider a higher cap on corporate income tax rebates than the current $20,000 cap for companies that record real productivity gains.

sections.label: Budget speech on cuts and firms
sections.summary: The speaker says the Industry Transformation Programme should identify double-weak firms and restrict their tax rebates and grants, and lists 20 cuts filed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To this end, the Industry Transformation Programme should identify and thereafter even prejudice firms that are what the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) calls "double-weak firms" – weak in having a Singaporean Core and weak in their commitment to fair hiring practices and the development of Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Likewise, these companies should be restricted from benefiting from corporate income tax rebates or tapping on the grants that go up on the business grants portal that is to be established in the fourth quarter of this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In this context, a deeper and more sophisticated public discussion on fiscal prudence, sustainability and accountability of Budget expenditure in a more ambiguous future becomes more and not less urgent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It is a Budget Statement about how everyone has a role to play and together, we will write the next chapters of the Singapore story.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This is a Budget which helps everyone but with a stronger focus on SMEs, our young, our low-wage workers, persons with disabilities (PwDs), our seniors and Institutions of Public Characters (IPCs).

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I initially wanted to focus this speech on the issues I filed cuts on; issues that I care about deeply and issues that fellow Singaporeans and residents have raised to me.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I filed 20 cuts altogether, raising concerns on how we can help single parents, young parents, the elderly, low-income families, micro-SMEs, drug offenders in their rehabilitation process, foreign workers, fighting climate change, the transboundary haze issue, improving flood management, moving towards a car-lite city, beefing up our Home Team, improving electronic waste recycling, expanding the Active, Beautiful, Clean (ABC) Waters Programme, extending the smoking prohibition, improving animal welfare, fighting wildlife trafficking and lastly, improving the OneService App.

sections.label: Public consultation feedback exercise
sections.summary: A public consultation exercise ran from 1 February to 26 February and received over 1,000 feedback responses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In this journey, we have asked fellow Singaporeans for their feedback through a public consultation exercise which started on 1 February and ended on 26 February.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Minister Heng had mentioned that we received over 1,000 feedback but, of course, I understand that not every feedback was received on the last day.

sections.label: Timing of first public consultation
sections.summary: The speaker suggests starting the first public consultation in November the previous year for one month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: For a financial year that starts in April, I suggest that we start the first public consultation in November the previous year for a period of one month.

sections.label: Feedback on babies and Budget concerns
sections.summary: The speaker reports feedback on babies born before 24 March 2016, Coney Island, PIC payouts and foreign worker levies, and hopes for a post-Budget consultation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The most feedback I have received is from the parents of the 93 babies born each day before 24 March 2016 when the new First Step Grant kicked in.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Some have even come to my Meet the People Sessions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: But there are questions on why 24 March, why not 1 January 2016, since the babies born from 1 January until 23 March 2016 missed out on the SG50 Baby Jubilee Gift and now the First Step Grant?

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: And so, I hope we can backdate it and provide the grant to babies born from 1st January 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: There are concerns on whether the development of Coney Island will affect the environment there.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: There are concerns on why we are lowering the cash payout rate for the Productivity and Innovation Credit (PIC) Scheme and proceeding with increasing the foreign worker levies for the services and construction sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I believe these are all valid concerns that we should look into and it is for that reason that I hope that for next year, we will include a public consultation phase after the Budget Statement is read and before the announcement of a final Budget.

sections.label: Automation Support Package details
sections.summary: The Automation Support Package includes a Capability Development Grant covering up to 50% of qualifying automation costs, an enhanced equipment loan and an Investment Allowance.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: With this Budget, the Automation Support Package, for example, has a Capability Development Grant, which can support up to 50% of qualifying costs for automation projects.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: The equipment loan is enhanced from 50% to 70% and the Investment Allowance is rather generous as well.

sections.label: Non-taxation of equity gains
sections.summary: The extension of the non-taxation of gain from equity is cited as a good example.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: The extension of the non-taxation of gain from equity is a good example.

sections.label: Productivity and Innovation Credit Scheme
sections.summary: The Productivity and Innovation Credit Scheme has boosted many companies, will be extended till 2018, and changes will follow.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: In this context the Productivity and Innovation Credit (PIC) Scheme has been a booster for many companies.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: It will be extended till 2018 and beyond that, there will some changes.

sections.label: SME Working Capital Loan
sections.summary: A new SME Working Capital Loan initiative has been announced to help maximise benefits.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Balance this also with another new initiative that has been announced, that is the SME Working Capital Loan to help maximise benefits.

sections.label: Unawareness of assistance schemes
sections.summary: Many are still not exposed to or unaware of available assistance schemes.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Many are still not exposed to or are unaware of available assistance schemes.

sections.label: MSF working with mosques
sections.summary: Another way will be for MSF to work with mosques to reach out to these families.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Another way will be for MSF to work with mosques to reach out to these families.

sections.label: Debt and credit cards
sections.summary: Some have eight to 10 credit cards, and some are forced to sell their homes because of debt and finances.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Some even have eight to 10 credit cards.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Some are forced to sell their homes because of debt and how they handled their finances.

sections.label: Education transforming families
sections.summary: Their children's generation can succeed because they are focused on education, the most important factor in transforming families' lives.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Their children's generation can succeed because they are focused on education, which is the most important factor in transforming the lives of their families.

sections.label: Middle-income schemes Budget omission
sections.summary: The Budget Statement made no mention of enhancing or expanding last year's middle-income schemes or introducing new ones.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Government was astute in recognising the problem and announced a slew of measures to help them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is interesting to note, however, that the Budget Statement this year made no mention of further enhancing or expanding the schemes targeted for the middle-income announced last year, let alone introduce new ones.
