sections.label: Soin unemployment insurance Medisave idea
sections.summary: Former NMP Dr Kanwaljit Soin suggested unemployment insurance using CPF Medisave, an idea worth exploring.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Former Nominated Member of Parliament (NMP), Dr Kanwaljit Soin, suggested unemployment insurance through the usage of Central Provident Fund's (CPF) Medisave, which seems to be an idea that is worth exploring.

sections.label: Budget silent on scheme enhancements
sections.summary: This year's Budget Statement did not state whether last year's schemes will be enhanced or expanded, or new ones introduced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Unfortunately, I find that this year's Budget Statement did not touch deeply on, and did not state, whether there will be further enhancements or expansions to the schemes announced last year, let alone introduce new schemes.

sections.label: Soin proposed unemployment insurance Medisave
sections.summary: Former NMP Dr Kanwaljit Soin proposed an unemployment insurance using the CPF Medisave account.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In fact, former NMP, Dr Kanwaljit Soin, proposed the idea of an unemployment insurance using the CPF Medisave account.

sections.label: Companies invest in R&D innovation
sections.summary: Over 30 years, the speaker observed that successful companies invest significantly in R&D and innovation activities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Through the 30 years, it is evidenced for me that successful companies invest significantly in R&D and innovation activities.

sections.label: Requests for continuous innovator supply
sections.summary: The speaker requests innovation curriculum, school competitions, mass media involvement, Ministerial stewardship and allocated funds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Herewith, I would like to request for the following if we are to create a continuous supply of innovators who can fit the strategic pieces: first, include innovation subject as part of the curriculum in primary schools up to tertiary institutions; second, nationwide and national level or cluster level innovation competition in schools, by the chambers of commerce, community organisations, and so on; third, mass media involvement to elevate these initiatives so as to create awareness and high-level interest in innovation; fourth, top level and Ministerial stewardship towards this innovation initiative; and, lastly, funds must be allocated for the above initiatives.

sections.label: Malay SMEs behind other ethnic SMEs
sections.summary: Malay SMEs are generally very far behind other ethnic SMEs in almost all areas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Without doubt, generally, Malay SMEs are very far behind other ethnic SMEs in almost all areas.

sections.label: Support for Malay SMEs
sections.summary: The speaker requests special attention and support for Malay SMEs and proposes a special business council, professional coaching and financial support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Malay SMEs need much more help if they are to move and meet the call in support of the nation's long-term strategic goals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Herewith, I would like to request to the relevant Ministries to render special attention to the plight of the Malay SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Amongst the few examples of two aspiring Malay SMEs that I know of which deserve and need all the support they can get are, first, Vector ScoreCard Pte Ltd run by Mr Nazri Muhamad; and, second, Enercon Asia Pte Ltd run by Mr Azhar Othman.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I believe there are more SMEs like them that have similar aspirations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is my hope to see SMEs like the above rise and become successful enterprises in the future with sales value of at least $220 million annually.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: They need to be guided and tap the professional expertise from experienced mentors who have the credentials of transforming SMEs into MNCs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Again, with this backdrop, I would like to propose the following: form a special business council within the Malay community to oversee and steer the progress of transforming possible Malay SMEs to reach a target annual revenue, to be determined and agreed upon, in support of the nation's strategic goal; providing the needed professional support so as to help the identified SMEs to meet its defined objectives; seek the assistance from the relevant Ministries if targeted SMEs could be given the support to have access and to be coached by top-level business consultants with the objective to grow our SMEs into MNCs; and, of course, lastly, financial support, which has already been outlined.

sections.label: Importance of SME support
sections.summary: SMEs form 99% of local businesses, create 70% of the labour force and contribute 50% of Singapore's GDP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The support given to small and medium enterprises (SMEs) is important because SMEs form 99% of all local businesses, creating 70% of the nation's labour force and contributing 50% towards Singapore's gross domestic product (GDP).

sections.label: Redundancy Insurance proposal
sections.summary: The speaker supports a Redundancy Insurance scheme funded by employers and workers to help involuntarily retrenched workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As one way to manage the impact of retrenchment that will certainly occur in the effort to achieve progress, I support my colleague Ms Sylvia Lim's suggestion that the Government consider introducing a Redundancy Insurance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This is an insurance scheme where employers and workers each contribute a small portion of the worker's monthly salary into a fund.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The objective of this fund is to help workers who are facing unemployment due to involuntary retrenchment, including those who were served notice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This fund can perhaps provide payouts over a period of six months, whereby the payout amount can be based on a small proportion of the last salary received by the worker, within the range of 40%, but at the same time, have a limit that is based on the median income.

sections.label: Extending schemes to all children
sections.summary: The speaker appeals to extend KidSTART and enhanced CDA schemes to every Singaporean child, including those born out of wedlock.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For this year's Budget, in an effort to aid early childhood development, a new initiative KidSTART was introduced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The present Child Development Account scheme (CDA) has been enhanced with an additional First Step grant of $3,000 as an initial assistance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: On the basis of this noble aim, I appeal to the Government to extend these schemes to every Singaporean child including those born out of wedlock.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Presently, Government schemes exclude this group of children.

sections.label: Student resilience and OBS
sections.summary: The speaker supports building the OBS in Coney Island to develop resilience and self-confidence in students.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The development of resilience among our students is important in preparing them for the various challenges in life and giving them self-confidence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I support the plan to build the OBS in Coney Island, which will be able to accommodate more participants.

sections.label: Link corporate entities with SSO
sections.summary: The speaker suggests establishing a more effective link or cooperation between corporate entities and individuals with the Social Service Office.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Here, I would like to suggest that we establish a more effective link or cooperation between corporate entities and individuals, with the Social Service Office (SSO).

sections.label: Good quality jobs for Singaporeans
sections.summary: The speaker says the 21st century must mean good quality jobs, with Singaporeans moving up the value chain and finding a branch of skills to specialise in.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: In the 21st century, this has to mean good quality jobs − Singaporeans moving up the value chain, climbing up the value tree, finding a branch of skills where they can specialise and find mastery.

sections.label: Avoiding pitfalls, securing opportunities
sections.summary: The speaker's second point is avoiding pitfalls while securing opportunities, noting Singapore evolved from a third-world to a first-world economy and low-hanging fruits are picked.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: My second point, Mdm Speaker, is avoiding pitfalls while securing opportunities.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: We have evolved from a third-world to a first-world economy, and the low-hanging fruits have already been picked.

sections.label: Incentives for MNCs to invest
sections.summary: The speaker cites a Harvard study on globalisation and says incentives are important for businesses, especially MNCs, to keep investing and reinvesting in Singapore and Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: The Harvard study also observed that, with globalisation, it is quite possible for a company, especially a multinational corporation (MNC), to grow more competitive, even if the host nation loses its edge, partly because of this lack of investment in the host country.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: So, Mdm Speaker, it is important that we provide incentives for businesses, especially MNCs, to continue investing in Singapore, and reinvesting in Singapore and Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: One way to do this is for companies to continue training up a strong Singaporean Core with skills and industry knowledge – not just the numbers, but people with skills and the tacit, implicit knowledge that comes from knowing an industry sector deeply and, especially, in business sectors of key importance where Singaporeans are still under-represented.

sections.label: Fiscal prudence and SkillsFuture
sections.summary: The speaker says fiscal prudence lets Government investment supplement this, and concurs that SkillsFuture is an important step forward.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: In Singapore, because of our history of fiscal prudence, we are in a position to supplement this with Government investment as well.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: And I concur with fellow Members that SkillsFuture is an important step forward, because individual companies, sometimes because of their size, may not be willing to underwrite the cost of training, or they may fear that a worker is going to move to another company after upskilling.

sections.label: GST supports progressive social programmes
sections.summary: The speaker says flat consumption taxes become overall progressive when revenue is redistributed, and describes how GST supports progressive social programmes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: So, you can have individual flat consumption taxes which, on their own, may be regarded as regressive by some observers, but when the revenue is redistributed to those with less and when it is used to help those who are disadvantaged, the system becomes overall progressive.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: This is how taxes like our Goods and Services Tax (GST) support progressive social programmes: (a) the GST Voucher Scheme, which helps families with less; (b) the upcoming Silver Support Scheme for elderly Singaporeans with fewer resources – sometimes just by accident of which era they were born in, they grew up earning third-world wages and retired in Singapore with often first-world costs; and (c) we see our Edusave Merit Bursaries, the MOE Financial Assistance Scheme.

sections.label: Charitable donation tax deductions
sections.summary: MOF is capping personal income tax relief, but the speaker says tax deductions for charitable donations should not be capped.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Our social norms and our social culture, they matter too.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: This is why even though the Ministry of Finance (MOF) is introducing a cap on the total amount of personal income tax relief, it is very important that we do not put a cap on tax deductions for charitable donations.

sections.label: Business and IPC Partnership Scheme
sections.summary: MOF will recognise employees giving time, services and secondments where they transfer skills and knowledge under the new scheme.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: The new Business and IPC Partnership Scheme, Mdm Speaker, is an important step forward.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: MOF is now going to recognise employees giving their time, services and even secondments where they transfer their skills and knowledge.

sections.label: Reducing complexity for vulnerable recipients
sections.summary: The speaker says complexity has regressive effects on the most vulnerable, so reducing complexity at the frontline matters.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: This can lead to a focus on the immediate present, to the detriment of the future and, as we have talked about, less time and energy available to navigate the different roads to help.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: So, it is important, Mdm Speaker, that we continue doing our best to reduce complexity, especially at the frontline and on the ground for the end-user or recipients of help, because complexity has regressive effects on the most vulnerable among us.

sections.label: Coordination at ground level
sections.summary: The speaker cites SSOs, SGfuture, Coordinating Ministers and frontline examples, and says coordination must be recognised and resourced.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: MSF's Social Service Offices (SSOs) and their coordinating roles have been a key step forward in coordinating care and helping families, especially those with deep complex issues who need a lot of attention to uplift them and make sure the children can continue getting a good start in life.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: The SGfuture programme is another platform to help people, Government, and agencies see issues together, co-create a future and especially look at issues through the eyes of the people.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: At our highest levels, we have our Coordinating Ministers looking after National Security, Economic and Social Policies, and Infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: But at the ground level, Madam, coordination matters very deeply as well – whether it is your family doctor, or a patient navigator in the hospital helping an elderly Singaporean find their way through the healthcare system; whether it is public servants seeing issues through the eyes of the end-user, working across departmental and agency boundaries, like our Municipal Services Office; or our social workers at our SSOs and the staff at the upcoming Community Networks for Seniors.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: So, Madam, in our policymaking and implementation, we must continue to recognise coordination as a valuable process and a valuable outcome, in and of itself.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: And we have to allocate resources and manpower to make sure coordination continues at the ground level and to keep things as simple as possible, especially for those starting with less and those who are disadvantaged.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Last week, the CEO of a cleaning company shared with me that they lost their cleaning contract with a Statutory Board this year because they had bid for the contract based on current salaries of their workers and also factored a one-month bonus.

sections.label: Wages at 20th and 50th percentiles
sections.summary: Gross wage at the 20th percentile is $1,800 and at the 50th percentile $3,460, with real wage growth of 2.1% versus 3%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In Singapore, the gross wage of workers at the 20th percentile is $1,800 while those at the 50th percentile is $3,460.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In the last five years, real wage increase for the 20th percentile was 2.1% compared to the higher percentage real wage increase for the 50th percentile at 3%.

sections.label: Workfare Income Supplement changes
sections.summary: The Labour Movement welcomes WIS changes letting more workers qualify with higher payouts, but wants a longer-term solution for low-wage workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In this Budget, the Labour Movement welcomes the changes made to the Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) to enable more workers to qualify with a higher payout, but we need a longer-term solution to help low-wage workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Potentially, we are looking at 85,000 local workers in these sectors benefiting from such a move.

sections.label: Longer contracts and PPP procurement
sections.summary: Calls for longer service contracts to encourage technology adoption and for Government to explore a PPP model in procuring essential services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Service buyers can also look into having contracts of longer duration to incentivise the service providers to embark on greater adoption of technology that could lead to manpower savings and better productivity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Relevant to my call for procurement process for outsourced services to be more worker centric, I would also like to call for the Government to explore a Public Private Partnership (PPP) model in procuring essential services such as cleaning, security and maintenance services.

sections.label: Discouraging Option to Extend
sections.summary: While calling for longer contract durations, it discourages having an Option to Extend on the same terms and conditions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: While I am calling for contracts to be of longer duration, I would like to discourage the practice of having an Option to Extend at the same terms and conditions.

sections.label: Welcoming Budget workfare changes
sections.summary: Welcomes the Budget's changes to the Workfare Income Supplement and Workfare Training Support schemes, which make more workers eligible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: (In Malay):   I welcome this year's Budget which aims to help the low-wage workers through changes made to the Workfare Income Supplement Scheme (WIS), and the Workfare Training Support (WTS) Scheme which will make more workers eligible.

sections.label: Malay workers using SkillsFuture
sections.summary: Says Malay workers, especially low-wage ones, should use SkillsFuture wisely given the $4.5 billion Industry Transformation Programme support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In view of the $4.5 billion support provided under the Industry Transformation Programme, it is important that Malay workers, especially the low-wage workers, make use of SkillsFuture wisely to ensure that the new skills that they learn will be useful to industries and companies which will be undergoing transformation through automation and technology, which will improve their productivity and reduce the demand for labour.

sections.label: Social indicators towards SG100
sections.summary: Lists social indicators raising support requirements: ageing population, income disparity, shrinking working population, and better-educated younger generation with higher aspirations.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: As we progress towards SG100, there are a few social indicators that will continue to raise the bar of support requirement in our society.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: These indicators are an increasing ageing population, constant need to bridge the income disparity, a shrinking working population and the well-educated younger generation with higher aspirations and expectations of what basic livelihood entails in a developed nation.

sections.label: Challenges facing social safety net
sections.summary: States three challenges: a more complex state support system, increasing funding needs requiring public cross-subsidies, and some groups still not qualifying for support.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: In order to supplement state support, we have further enhanced our social safety net for those more vulnerable through multiple schemes.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: However, the challenges that we face are: one, the state support system has become more complex over the years and it is harder to implement with ease so as to maximise the support for the intended beneficiaries; two, increasing funding requirements means a need for the public to cross-subsidise in different ways; and three, some groups, albeit small in quantity, may still not qualify for any available support schemes.

sections.label: Pioneer Generation Package seniors
sections.summary: The Pioneer Generation Package began in 2015 and was crucial for seniors with lower preparedness to manage healthcare costs.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Pioneer Generation Package (PGP) began in 2015 and that was crucial to many seniors due to their age and also the lower preparedness to manage their healthcare costs as they started their lives during the difficult times of nation building.

sections.label: Silver Support and future seniors
sections.summary: Silver Support gives quarterly payouts to bottom seniors, but the next generation of seniors will likely need similar support at higher cost.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: It was critical for the lower income families and those with little savings to manage their hospital care needs.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Now, there is the Silver Support Scheme providing quarterly payouts for the bottom 20% of seniors and, to some extent, 30% of them.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: While all these are beneficial to our Pioneer Generation (PGs), their children who are the next generation of seniors will likely require the same types of support but at a much higher cost than our PGs today.

sections.label: Targeted subsidies and self-sufficiency
sections.summary: No system covers all groups, so support is targeted, raising the question of whether those assumed self-sufficient can manage alone.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: The reality of any system is it cannot provide coverage for all groups across the society, thus, the need to dispense support based on a targeted approach.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: However, if subsidies continue to be targeted only for specific groups, how can we be assured that those whom we believe are self-sufficient will indeed be able to manage on their own?

sections.label: Integrated Social Hub 3G Village
sections.summary: The speaker proposed an Integrated Social Hub, or 3G Village, and noted Budget 2016 focuses on last mile delivery and social innovation.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Earlier in my maiden speech, I spoke about the need for an Integrated Social Hub, or what I term the the 3G Village, where we can bring community networks together and reinforce social values through inter-generational sharing, thereby strengthening our social fabric.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: It is heartening to note that in Budget 2016, more focus is given to improve last mile delivery and social innovation to maximise impact of schemes.

sections.label: SG Future Citizen Engagements
sections.summary: The speaker hopes SG Future Ministries continue partnering the community to co-create solutions and deliver services effectively in the digital age.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Lastly, to expand on the SG Future Citizen Engagements that was launched in November 2015, I hope the various SG Future Ministries continue to partner the community in co-creating solutions and finding more effective methods of delivering their services in this digital age.

sections.label: State support with community involvement
sections.summary: State support with individual, family and community involvement is the way forward for a basic decent standard of living for all Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: State support coupled with individuals, family and community involvement is the way forward to ensure a basic decent standard of living for all Singaporeans, even as the cost of that invariably rises over time.

sections.label: Budget 2016 cost-of-living support measures
sections.summary: Budget 2016 provides measures supporting cost-of-living expenses, including GST vouchers, MediShield Life subsidies and the Silver Support Scheme for seniors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Budget 2016 provides for many measures that support our cost-of-living expenses such as the GST vouchers and other top-ups, support and subsidies for various schemes such as MediShield Life to prepare us for our long-term healthcare costs, and the Silver Support Scheme, for seniors who may need support in their retiring years.

sections.label: Review policies affecting retirement security
sections.summary: It says savings went into long-term interest payments and indirect taxes like housing levies, and calls for an end-to-end review of retirement security policies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This is also exacerbated because a large part of their savings had also gone into long-term interest payments and other indirect taxes such as housing levies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I think we are too deep in after many years to reverse the use of the CPF for housing, but on the broader scale of our collective policies, the Government should consider an end-to-end review of our policies that affect retirement security and whether they are sufficient to give Singaporeans a strong sense of security in old age.

sections.label: CPF LIFE and Minimum Sum
sections.summary: It states CPF LIFE is a big improvement, but the Minimum Sum remains a moving target to many.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: CPF LIFE is certainly a big improvement, but the Minimum Sum is still a moving target to many.

sections.label: Silver Support Scheme excludes larger flat residents
sections.summary: It says the Silver Support Scheme leaves out senior citizens in 5-room flats or larger, leaving many middle-income retirees unsupported.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The Silver Support Scheme, for instance, was implemented with good intentions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: However, leaving out senior citizens who are in 5-room flats or larger, does leave many retirees who were middle-income earners, unsupported.

sections.label: Means-testing and Silver Support criteria
sections.summary: It argues means-testing this way no longer reflects wealth or income, and calls the household-type criterion archaic and diminishing to the scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: So, means-testing this way no longer makes sense as a reflection of wealth or income status.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: We accept means-testing in welfare schemes and hospital subsidies but let us also take a practical approach on other schemes such as Silver Support Scheme, especially in helping our retirees, as they are no longer working or earning an income.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The inclusion of the second criterion using household types is an archaic idea that diminishes the impact of the scheme.

sections.label: Clarity and transparency in social compact
sections.summary: It says clarity and greater transparency in the social compact are important, since funding schemes people cannot use or benefit from is pointless.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: It is important to ensure that there is clarity and greater transparency in our social compact.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: There is no point pouring millions of dollars into schemes that people do not know how to use or know that they can benefit from, or they can leverage.

sections.label: Taxi and bus drivers
sections.summary: The passage asks what will be done with thousands of taxi, bus and goods vehicle drivers in future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: What do we do with the thousands of taxi drivers, bus drivers, goods vehicle drivers in time to come?

sections.label: SkillsFuture and industrial policy
sections.summary: SkillsFuture leaves much to personal choice, so a clear concerted industrial policy may be needed as the Government studies future technologies and jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: SkillsFuture is a wonderful initiative, but it also leaves a lot to personal choice and therefore may not be able to shape the momentum and direction of our labour force.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: A clear and concerted industrial policy may be needed, given that the Government has been studying the development of these technologies and the jobs of the future.

sections.label: PMET workers and automation
sections.summary: The passage states that some workers, including the PMET segment, may become less relevant due to automation and artificial intelligence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Within this wave, certain workers, including the PMET segment, may become less relevant due to automation and the use of artificial intelligence.

sections.label: Digital platforms and media competition
sections.summary: Digital platforms like Netflix and Spotify bring competition to MediaCorp, Singtel and Starhub, so people must reinvent themselves and use SkillsFuture to upskill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In media, digital platforms like Netflix and Spotify also brings competition to current media platforms like MediaCorp, Singtel and Starhub, and all these affect us.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: We need to reinvent ourselves, and make use of SkillsFuture to upskill or look for new skills.

sections.label: Malay bodies implementing programmes
sections.summary: The passage hopes MUIS, Mendaki and AMP will help implement programmes and enhance efforts for the community to embrace technology in the digital era.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Here, I hope that Malay bodies like MUIS, Mendaki and the Association of Muslim Professionals (AMP) will play a part in implementing several programmes, and we should further enhance the efforts to help the community undergo this transformation to embrace technology in the digital era.

sections.label: Lee Kuan Yew rainbow quote
sections.summary: The passage recalls Lee Kuan Yew's quote about looking at the horizon and riding the rainbow, and says giving people security matters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Twenty years ago, our late founding father Mr Lee Kuan Yew made a famous quote, "To the young and the not so old, I say, look at the horizon, follow the rainbow and go ride it." Madam, I believe in the rainbow, and it is important to give our people a sense of security for the future.

sections.label: Riding the rainbow of opportunities
sections.summary: The passage states that only then can Singaporeans be more confident to ride the rainbow of opportunities that come with this nation they call home.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Only then can we be more confident to ride the rainbow of opportunities that come with this great nation that we call home.

sections.label: Slow growth and manufacturing decline
sections.summary: Growth last year was 2.1%, the slowest since 2009, with economists expecting around 2% for the next few years, and manufacturing declined 5.2%.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Our growth last year of 2.1% was the slowest since 2009 and economists expect growth for the next few years to remain stuck at around 2%.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Manufacturing actually declined by 5.2% last year, again, the worst showing since the global financial crisis.

sections.label: Productivity push not on track
sections.summary: Reports suggest that the push to increase productivity by 2% to 3% is not on track.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Macro-economically, reports suggest that our push to increase productivity by 2% to 3% is not on track.

sections.label: From PIC grants to Automation Support Package
sections.summary: Many companies bought machineries that are still lying unused, so the transition from PIC grants to the Automation Support Package is the right way to go.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In the past few years, many companies put up websites, bought machineries, some of which are still lying at a corner of their office and collecting dust.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Hence, the transition from PIC grants to the Automation Support Package is the right way to go.

sections.label: Strengthening trade associations with grants
sections.summary: Strengthening trade associations with grants and seconded Government officers is timely, as trade associations know the needs and challenges of their industries.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The idea of strengthening trade associations with grants and seconded Government officers is also a timely one, as trade associations are the ones who knows the needs and challenges of their respective industries.

sections.label: Automation definition and retrenchment concerns
sections.summary: The automation definition should not be too narrow, and companies should retain as many Singaporeans as possible, including in high-income jobs.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: First, when the automation support package replaces PIC, the definition of automation should not be too narrow, because this will make application more difficult, or it may miss investments that could truly increase productivity.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: (In English): Mdm Speaker, the third issue is retrenchment.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We need to make sure companies try to retain as many Singaporeans as possible, including in high-income jobs.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Do not cut the locals from management jobs, while retaining lower-paid locals to fulfil the quotas.

sections.label: Tax burden on working mothers
sections.summary: A mother said the cap will raise her tax burden by 20%, and she is reconsidering quitting work.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: One such mother told me that this will increase her tax burden by 20%.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: She is already feeling stress from juggling her work, kids and parents, and is now even re-considering quitting the workforce to focus on her family.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I know this cap is expected to net $100 million a year in revenue, but I certainly hope it will not turn out to be "penny wise, pound foolish" by driving high-income mothers away from the workforce or reducing the number of children they add to our future workforce.

sections.label: Having babies for country's survival
sections.summary: The speaker says without a mindset change, having more babies is for the country's survival, and packages may not achieve the outcome.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: So, if there is no change in mindset, 传宗接代, to have more babies is for the survival of the country.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I do not think all these packages that we are dishing out are going to give us the desired outcome.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Our Minister for Finance has a very challenging balancing act to perform.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: He needs to do an admirable balance between generosity and prudence, between short-term support and long-term development.

sections.label: HDB shops benefitting from scheme
sections.summary: As of March 2016, the HDB website stated the scheme has benefitted 4,600 shops at 54 sites.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: As of March 2016, the HDB website stated that the scheme has benefitted 4,600 shops at 54 sites.

sections.label: HDB spending on ROS scheme
sections.summary: Mr Lee Yi Shyan said HDB has spent $8.4 million since the ROS scheme was introduced in 2007.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In last year's Committee of Supply (COS) debate in March 2015, former Senior Minister of State for National Development, Mr Lee Yi Shyan, said that HDB has spent $8.4 million since the ROS scheme was introduced in 2007.

sections.label: Increased funding for ROS scheme
sections.summary: Budget 2016 sets aside $15 million annually for the ROS scheme, over 10 times the previous average expenditure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Budget 2016 will set aside $15 million annually to enhance the ROS scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This is a large increase compared to previous years, more than 10 times the average expenditure in previous years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: While I am sure it is good that our existing HDB shops are receiving more assistance to enhance their businesses, I hope the Minister for Finance can share the reasons for this large annual increase in funding for the scheme and also share details about how the proposed increase in funding will be utilised, and in what ways will the coming year's programme be different from the past.

sections.label: Retrenched PMETs driving taxis
sections.summary: Retrenched PMETs from SMEs or MNCs resorted to driving taxis full-time or part-time to supplement incomes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Many PMETs who were retrenched from their jobs with both SMEs or MNCs had to resort to driving taxis as a full-time job as they were not able to find suitable replacement jobs or, for others, who were only able to find jobs where the income offered was much less than their previous incomes, they had to resort to driving taxis on a part-time basis to supplement their incomes.

sections.label: Adapt and Grow Initiative
sections.summary: Government measures like Adapt and Grow and TechSkills Accelerator should help use the working population's productive capacity to some extent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In this regard, measures announced by the Government, such as the Adapt and Grow Initiative and TechSkills Accelerator, should be able to facilitate the utilisation of the productive capacity of the working population to a certain extent.

sections.label: Retrenchment insurance payouts
sections.summary: Retrenchment insurance would give a retrenched worker a payout for a few months before finding a new job.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: If workers can be provided with retrenchment insurance, in the event of retrenchment, he can receive financial assistance by way of a payout from such insurance policy for say a few months before he finds a new job.

sections.label: Child CDA $3,000
sections.summary: Parents automatically receive $3,000 in their child's CDA for healthcare and childcare needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Parents will automatically receive $3,000 in their child's CDA which they can use for their children's healthcare and childcare needs.

sections.label: New OBS campus Coney Island
sections.summary: The Government proposes a national outdoor adventure education masterplan to build a new Outward Bound Singapore campus on Coney Island.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Under this section, the Government is making a single proposal that through a new national outdoor adventure education masterplan, it will build a new Outward Bound Singapore (OBS) campus on Coney Island.

sections.label: Resilience in life's race
sections.summary: Resilience is pushing on through cramps, shin splints or retrenchment rather than sitting and despairing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: You can plan to run each kilometre of your race in five or six minutes, but you will never know whether you are going to get the cramps at 33 kilometres which will throw your marathon race into disarray.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Resilience is when you are down with cramps at 33 kilometres and you keep pushing to cross the finishing line and not give up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Resilience is when you are down with shin splints but still work on your recovery to get back to finish your race another day.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: When the chips are down, when you are struggling with your business or when you are laid off by the MNC you work with for 20 years, what do you do in the race of life?

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Do you just sit and despair or do you pick yourself up and press on to cross the finishing line another day?

sections.label: R&D, JID, robotics initiatives
sections.summary: The $4 billion R&D funding, Jurong Innovation District and robotics initiative aim to move ideas to market and strengthen start-ups and SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: One, the $4 billon R&D funding for industry research collaboration is a big step to push the best ideas out of the labs and into the marketplace.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Two, Jurong Innovation District (JID) is a strong move to strengthen our start-up eco-system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Three, our robotics initiative helps our SMEs get ahead of the curve, to be active disruptors, rather than passive bystanders in the coming era of robots and machines.

sections.label: ITM for HDB retail sector
sections.summary: The Government can consider developing an ITM for the HDB retail sector, with HDB, NEA, Town Councils, SPRING Singapore and the Federation of Merchants' Associations partnering.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Fourth, the Government can consider developing an ITM for the HDB retail sector as well.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: They face different challenges compared to the rest of the retail sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I hope that HDB, the National Environmental Agency (NEA) and even Town Councils, as major regulators of our heartlands, can partner with SPRING Singapore and the Federation of Merchants' Associations of Singapore, to drive this important effort.

sections.label: Partnership and Government industry leadership
sections.summary: Increasing partnership intensity and working as one Team Singapore strengthens success odds, and the Government will provide industry leadership to sectors like F&B and retail.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This may not sound significant, but increasing the intensity of the partnership and working as one Team Singapore, will strengthen our odds for success in an exponential manner.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It is also groundbreaking because the Government will provide much needed industry leadership to sectors which usually lack clear and holistic Government direction, such as the F&B and retail sectors.

sections.label: Budget and skills-based economy
sections.summary: This Budget continues to help Singapore evolve to a skills-based economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: One, this Budget continues to help us evolve to a skills-based economy.

sections.label: Budget balance companies and workers
sections.summary: This Budget strikes a fine balance between companies and the Singaporean worker.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Two, this Budget strikes a fine balance between companies and the Singaporean worker.

sections.label: Budget support for older workers and construction
sections.summary: This Budget encourages companies to hire older Singaporeans as they re-skill and provides a lifeline for Singaporeans in private sector construction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Three, this Budget continues the Government's efforts to encourage companies to hire older Singaporeans as they re-skill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Four, this Budget helps provide a lifeline for many Singaporeans involved in private sector construction.

sections.label: Fall in exports and manufacturing recession
sections.summary: Singapore's January non-oil domestic export fell 9.9% year on year, and manufacturing, a fifth of the economy, declined 5.2% in 2015.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: In February this year, it was reported that Singapore's January non-oil domestic export fell 9.9% compared with the same month last year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The manufacturing sector of Singapore has been in recession for a year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: This sector which makes up a fifth of Singapore's economy has been hit hardest with a decline last year of 5.2% from 2014, its worst performance in 14 years.

sections.label: Rising layoffs and redundancies
sections.summary: 15,580 workers were laid off last year, a 20% rise from 2014 and the highest since 2009, the fifth straight year of rising redundancies.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Although Minister Heng said that unemployment is still low, it is nonetheless a total of 15,580 workers being laid off last year, the fifth year in a row that redundancies rose.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Last year's number climbed 20% from 2014 and was the highest since 2009.

sections.label: Incentives for part-time work
sections.summary: Companies could be incentivised to keep staff through part-time work arrangements instead of retrenchments when cutting costs in the current economic climate.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Companies could be incentivised to keep their staff with part-time work arrangements rather than retrenchments when they need to cut costs due to the present economic climate.

sections.label: Jobs Credit Scheme for SMEs
sections.summary: The speaker asks if MOF will consider the Jobs Credit Scheme again for SMEs, describing its 12% cash grants and suggesting tweaks.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Will MOF also consider the Jobs Credit Scheme again for SMEs, especially if the situation worsens with even more redundancies, and encourage our companies to preserve jobs?

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Employers received 12% cash grants on the first $2,500 of each month's wages for each employee on their CPF payroll.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: It was a good scheme and should be considered again, if necessary, but with some tweaks in enforcement.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: We can consider crediting the cash grants to the employees directly rather than to the companies whilst allowing corresponding adjustments to the employee salaries by the companies.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Another tweak that can be considered would be the coupling of job credit with skills upgrading by recipients as an eligibility requirement.

sections.label: MOM measures for workforce segment
sections.summary: In July last year, MOM announced measures to support this segment of the workforce.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: In July last year, MOM announced a number of measures to support this segment of the workforce.

sections.label: Automation Support Package funding
sections.summary: The Automation Support Package aims to spend over $400 million in the next three years to help firms scale up automation projects.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The Automation Support Package aims to spend over $400 million in the next three years to support firms in scaling up their automation projects.

sections.label: Outdoor adventure education masterplan
sections.summary: The Budget intends a masterplan for outdoor adventure education to develop ruggedness and resilience in youth, which the speaker finds heartening.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In an earlier speech I made in response to the President's Address, I spoke about the importance of imbuing our youth with the psychological capital to persevere in the face of setbacks, and the need to introduce experiential learning components into our schools' formal curriculum.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: It is thus heartening to know that this year's Budget intends to put in place a masterplan for outdoor adventure education, with the aim of developing ruggedness and resilience in our youth.

sections.label: Silver Support Scheme qualifying criteria
sections.summary: The scheme does not tie payouts to work or active contribution, and the speaker asks if the Finance Ministry could consider cases in obvious need that may not qualify under broad criteria.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: What is radical about this scheme is that it does not tie the payout to "work" or any form of active contribution or participation on the part of the elderly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The Silver Support Scheme will thus not only help these elderly who qualify, but also their family members by alleviating the family's overall financial commitments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I understand the need to keep the qualifying criteria simple and straightforward, so that the scheme can be administered fairly quickly without the need for too much analysis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: However, I would like to ask if the Finance Ministry could also consider certain cases that are in obvious need of help, but might not qualify for the scheme based on these broad criteria.

sections.label: Mental wellness stigma and support
sections.summary: Mental wellness remains stigmatised in Singapore, and the speaker suggests a decentralised approach to build awareness and make mental health support more accessible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Unfortunately, Sir, mental wellness is still very much stigmatised in Singapore where Singaporeans would often equate a visit to the Institute of Mental Health (IMH) with schizophrenia or some other catastrophic mental health issue.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Indeed, many of my residents still colloquially refer to the IMH as "Siao-Lang Keng" or the "Insane Asylum." Perhaps a decentralised approach to mental wellness could be a better way to build community awareness around stress management and mild depression, and this will also encourage residents who need such services to be more receptive to getting help.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I believe this is important as providing easily accessible mental health support would be increasingly important for our society as Singaporeans search for more ways to cope with the stress of living in a fast-paced society, and to also better manage and negotiate the economic challenges that are coming our way.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: It is a conservative and balanced one that has addressed economic concerns while acknowledging the need for measured and sustainable social spending.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: It is heartening to know that the Government has recognised the importance of experiential learning for our youth and will make significant investments in this direction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I also hope that more attention can be given to improving the "heart-ware" infrastructure to provide more support for the vulnerable members in our community.

sections.label: Budget 2016 innovation theme
sections.summary: Budget 2016 declares "Transformation through Innovation" as the best way forward.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Budget 2016 declares "Transformation through Innovation" as our best way forward.

sections.label: Matching roadmaps for people's transformation
sections.summary: Sustained industry transformation should be matched with bespoke roadmaps for the long-term psychological and emotional transformation of people.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: If we want sustained transformation of our industries, we should be drawing up matching bespoke roadmaps for the long-term psychological and emotional transformation of our people as well.

sections.label: Culture and collaboration in Singapore
sections.summary: Understanding why collaboration is difficult in Singapore requires tracking behaviours and attitudes on openness and trust, matching strategy with culture.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And if we want to know why collaboration does not happen easily in Singapore, we have to track our behaviours and attitudes surrounding openness and trust.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We must match "Strategy with Culture." If you want to see strategies succeed, cultural intervention must always be the first resort.

sections.label: SGInnovate pairing strategy with culture
sections.summary: If SGInnovate is tasked to cultivate an innovation ecosystem, it must pair strategic matchmaking with culture-building efforts connected to its goals.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: If SGInnovate is being tasked to cultivate an ecosystem for innovation, it has to pair its strategic matchmaking with culture-building efforts that connect with its goals.

sections.label: SGInnovate and local early adopters
sections.summary: SGInnovate must find local early adopters of innovation culture and work with them to build Singapore's thought leadership on innovation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: SGInnovate must seek out the local early adopters of innovation culture and work with them to help build up Singapore's thought leadership on innovation.

sections.label: Kiasu culture and grantrepreneurs
sections.summary: The passage describes parents buying unproductive pre-school tuition and says kiasu culture created grantrepreneurs who chase public monies like the PIC grant.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Straits Times discovered four in 10 parents purchase tuition for pre-schoolers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And when asked why, the overriding reason, of course, was better grades.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But in the same breath, only a third of these parents said tuition actually improves academic performance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So, by their own admission, they are paying for something that they already admit is not productive.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The price is the time and money that could have been spent developing their child in more worthwhile skills. "Kiasu" culture is too costly a culture to put up with and there are huge trade-offs in human development, manpower and time and dollars spent. "Kiasu" culture is also what created the subculture of grantrepreneurs – people who call themselves entrepreneurs but are really just grant-chasers – who seize upon any kind of public monies, like the PIC grant, to use on everything but what the grant was meant to accomplish.

sections.label: Jackpot Auntie giving to charity
sections.summary: The passage cites the Jackpot Auntie who gave away her $0.5 million casino windfall twice to charity, saying she had all she wanted.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So, I'm able to want you to have enough too".

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is what allowed that famous "Jackpot Auntie" to give away her casino windfall of $0.5 million not once, but twice to charity.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And when reporters asked her why she would do something like that when she was not rich, she said, "I have all that I want".

sections.label: Benefits for single unwed mums
sections.summary: The passage asks for single unwed mums and their children to get the same benefits as married mothers, and notes the CDA First Step Grant for all Singapore babies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: At last year's Budget, I asked that we consider giving single unwed mums and their children the same benefits and acceptance we accord to married mothers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: MSF has already announced that they will review the inequalities in policies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We are struggling with birth rates, so it is right that all young life that has been given to Singapore should be duly welcomed and all their life-bearers duly honoured.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This year, Minister Heng mentioned "all" Singapore babies will receive the Child Development Account (CDA) First Step Grant that can help struggling parents access the State's generous co-savings plan.

sections.label: Yellow Ribbon and second prison
sections.summary: The passage cites the Yellow Ribbon Project as moral leadership and calls for unlocking everyone's second prison of shame.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Government led the way before when it created the Yellow Ribbon Project that taught us a better way of seeing the ex-offenders in our midst, and that was courageous moral leadership we can all get behind.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Sometimes, you just have to commit the crime of being somehow second-class in people's eyes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So, let us unlock everyone's second prison of shame.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Let us spend the next 50 years charting our course towards becoming truly wealthy." Our unity has always been our greatest source of wealth.

sections.label: Fortunes built on promises
sections.summary: The passage states fortunes can come and go but can be rebuilt on promises between husbands and wives, parents and children, haves and have-nots, governments and people.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Fortunes can come and go but they can be built up again on the bedrock of a thousand strong promises made between husbands and wives, parents and children, haves and have-nots, governments and their people.

sections.label: Support for Budget and unity
sections.summary: The speaker says coming problems are probably bigger than thought and supports the Budget and call to greater unity.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So, yes, the problems that are coming are probably bigger and more powerful than we think.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I support your Budget and your call to greater unity.

sections.label: Workfare income ceiling raised
sections.summary: The speaker supports raising the Workfare Income Supplement qualifying income ceiling from $1,900 to $2,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: It is critical that a caring Government continues to help the less advantaged in an affluent society.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: I support the fact that the Government is raising the qualifying income ceiling for Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) from $1,900 to $2,000.

sections.label: Workfare payout increases supported
sections.summary: The speaker supports WIS payout increases between $100 and $500 to help recipients reach financial independence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: We can be more generous in giving them a boost or a leg up to eventually achieve financial independence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: I also support the fact that WIS payout would see increases between $100 and $500.

sections.label: Seniors criteria and housing type
sections.summary: The Minister for Finance said three criteria identify low-income seniors, and the speaker urges excluding housing type.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: The Minister for Finance had announced that the Government will use three criteria in combination to identify those seniors who are low-income or without income and are at the bottom 20% to 30% of the seniors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: These criteria are lifetime wages, housing type and level of household support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: I hope to urge the Minister to reconsider and exclude the criterion of housing type.

sections.label: Industry Transformation Programme launched
sections.summary: The Government launched a $4.5 billion Industry Transformation Programme to strengthen enterprises and industries and drive innovation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: The Government has launched a $4.5 billion Industry Transformation Programme (ITP) to strengthen enterprises and industries, and to drive growth through innovation.

sections.label: Retrenchment benefit law proposed
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Government will consider a law compelling retrenching companies to pay three to six months of benefits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Some of these workers are also upset that having served their employers faithfully for several years, when the company downsizes the operations and has to retrench staff, no consideration is given to the staff for their loyalty or their efforts in building up the company.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: So, I ask the Government: will the Government consider introducing a retrenchment benefit law that would compel companies that retrench staff to pay a minimum of between three and six months of retrenchment benefits depending on the length of service by the staff?

sections.label: Compulsory retrenchment benefits for all staff
sections.summary: Retrenchment benefits should be compulsory rather than left to agreement or discretion, and should cover all staff including PMETs and management.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: The payment for retrenchment benefits should be made compulsory instead of leaving it to agreement between employer or employee or leaving it to becoming discretionary.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: It should also apply to all staff including PMETs and management.

sections.label: Retrenchment benefit laws in other countries
sections.summary: Many other countries like Australia and the UK have laws requiring companies to pay retrenchment benefits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Many other countries like Australia and the UK have laws requiring companies to pay retrenchment benefits.

sections.label: Urging Government to explore retrenchment option
sections.summary: Details can be worked out by reference to other countries and a cap can be imposed, so the Government is urged to explore this option.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Details can be worked out by reference to the amount paid in other countries and the Government can always impose a cap on the amount of retrenchment benefits to be paid.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: So, I urge the Government to explore this option.

sections.label: Means-testing criteria need calibration and review
sections.summary: Some question the support they feel they deserve and missed out on, so means-testing criteria need careful calibration and constant review.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Some question the support they feel they deserve and missed out on because of existing criteria.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I think the means-testing criteria is something that needs to be carefully calibrated, and constantly reviewed to ensure that people who need help are not left to fend for themselves.

sections.label: Partnership means shared responsibility
sections.summary: Partnership means doing our part and sharing responsibility between the Government and the people.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Partnership means we have to do our part; it means that there must be shared responsibility between the Government and the people.

sections.label: Tapping Our Singapore Fund for community projects
sections.summary: There is a great opportunity to tap on Our Singapore Fund to come up with projects that can help the community.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: In particular, there is a great opportunity to tap on Our Singapore Fund to come up with projects that can help the community.

sections.label: Economy innovation enterprise strategy
sections.summary: The Minister for Finance laid out a strategy to transform the economy through innovation and enterprise.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: The Minister for Finance laid out the strategy to transform our economy through innovation and enterprise.

sections.label: Lower-income families and change
sections.summary: Rapid technological changes and global competition will affect lower-income families most.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: In the face of rapid technological changes and global competition, families from the lower-income group will be affected most.

sections.label: Three thrusts for transformation
sections.summary: The speaker sees three thrusts: target the young, support the family, and build social capital.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I am of the view that to move the needle, there is a need to transform our approach.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I see three main thrusts in this effort: one, target the young; two, continued support for the family; three, focus on building social capital.

sections.label: Approaches to enhance social mobility
sections.summary: The speaker recommends coordinated interaction between diverse students and a community support network.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I believe this is a key component in enhancing social mobility.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I recommend that we look at two approaches: one, coordinated interaction between students from diverse background and two, creating a community network of support.

sections.label: Peer mentoring and community network
sections.summary: Peer mentoring could be a scholarship condition, and a community network could pool accessible resources.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: In addition, this peer mentoring component could be something that we can incorporate as a condition or requirement in scholarships in appropriate circumstances.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Another effort we can make is the creation of a community network of support with various VWOs, businesses and partners, so that there can be a pool of resources which is easily accessible to those from the lower-income background.

sections.label: Reviewing assistance criteria
sections.summary: Criteria for assistance must be reviewed constantly so those facing difficulties do not feel trapped.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: The criteria established for the provision of assistance must be reviewed constantly so that those facing difficulties will not feel trapped.

sections.label: Schemes and Singaporeans' wellbeing
sections.summary: Government schemes can help Singaporeans prepare for economic structural changes and new jobs, but only if their body, hearts and spirits are also considered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Government schemes can help Singaporeans prepare for structural changes in our economy, and to move into new jobs and responsibilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, schemes will only help Singaporeans if we also look at how our body, hearts and spirits are affected in these moments of change, crisis and loss.

sections.label: Arts absent from Budget
sections.summary: The arts are not mentioned in this year's Budget, not even in the section on transforming the economy through enterprise and innovation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: To further reinforce that concern is the fact that the arts are not mentioned in this year's Budget.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Surprisingly, the arts does not even get a mention in the section "Transforming our economy through enterprise and innovation".

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This, despite the fact that the arts powers innovation, which is important if we are to be future-ready in challenging times.

sections.label: Equitable, viable, sustainable transformation
sections.summary: The transformation of the economy through innovation should also be equitable, viable and sustainable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: While we want to transform our economy through innovation, we also want the transformation to be equitable, viable and sustainable.

sections.label: State mediation and forced beliefs
sections.summary: The state has failed in mediation techniques, being reactive and unable to manage difference, so a few complaints can lead to an artwork or book being removed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: What if one group were to force their opinions and belief systems on others?

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I say this because, in many ways, the state has failed in mediation techniques.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is reactive, unable to effectively manage difference to find a common ground.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For example, a few letters complaining about an artwork or a book may lead to that work or book being removed.

sections.label: Art in school education
sections.summary: Art should be part of school education, so MOE and MCCY are asked to invest more in creative and critical teaching.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Art should be very much a part of our education in school.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Hence, I would like to request our Ministry of Education (MOE) and the Ministry for Culture, Community and Youth (MCCY) to invest more in creative and critical teaching.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Educators cannot facilitate creative and critical learning if schools do not allow themselves to be laboratories of learning and laboratories of knowledge.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Nowadays, we go to school and learn so that we can get prepared for our careers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In Chinese, we call it the pursuit of 学业。学了就 业, that is, "Learn and you get a job".

sections.label: Space for discourse
sections.summary: Without opening up the space for discourse, Singapore will never become a nation of mature thinkers and innovators.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: If the space for discourse is not going to be opened up, we will never become a nation of mature thinkers and innovators.

sections.label: Arts as safe space
sections.summary: The arts have for centuries provided a safe space to ask questions, understand one another and dream of a diverse communal future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Our literature, our music, our painting, our theatre, our cultural sites like Bukit Brown and many other tangible and intangible heritage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For centuries, the arts have provided a safe space for us to ask questions, understand one another better, and dream of a better communal future that embraces diversity.

sections.label: Support for seniors and families
sections.summary: Seniors get Silver Support payouts, needy households more cash assistance, and families with children benefit from First Step, KidSTART and Fresh Start grants.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Many seniors will be assisted through the Silver Support payouts, needy households will get more cash assistance and families with children will benefit from First Step, KidSTART and the Fresh Start grants.

sections.label: Time bank for seniors
sections.summary: A time bank could let seniors deposit volunteering hours and exchange them for privileges like queue priority, PA courses or an LPA fee waiver.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: One possibility is a time bank, whereby every hour of volunteering clocked by participating seniors can be deposited, accumulated and exchanged for certain privileges such as priority in queues at polyclinics and public hospitals, free or discounted People's Association (PA) courses, or even a waiver of the $50 application fee for the Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA) after the fee waiver expires this September.

sections.label: National Steps Challenge launch
sections.summary: The authorities launched the National Steps Challenge initiative last year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Last year, the authorities launched the National Steps Challenge initiative.

sections.label: Support for women and caregivers
sections.summary: The speaker seeks preventive care support for women, help for grandparents choosing between work and caregiving, and lifting the tax relief cap for divorced or widowed mothers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Women also live longer than men, although a significant portion of their final days may be in poor health.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I hope that MOH will consider new measures to provide more support to women, especially homemakers, in the area of preventive care.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: With the retirement age increasing to 67, more grandparents will have to choose between work and looking after grandchildren.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
