sentences.text: While a grandparent will probably earn more working outside, such a rebate will help lessen the financial sacrifice if the grandparent is inclined to look after the child herself or himself, especially when the child is an infant or very young.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: So far, there has been no limit on the total amount of personal income tax reliefs an individual taxpayer can claim.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: This change will affect working mothers with higher incomes the most because of the tax reliefs that they get from the Working Mother's Child Relief.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Granted, these women earn high incomes but I would like to appeal for the cap to be lifted for those who are divorced or widowed as they usually face more challenges such as raising families on their own.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Many of these women hold senior positions in their demanding careers and have to juggle pressing family needs as well.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I hope the Minister will take into account their extenuating circumstances.

sections.label: Support for economic transformation
sections.summary: The speaker supports the direction and measures to catalyse economic transformation and strengthen capabilities so Singapore is less dependent on foreign manpower.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Building on, I would like to offer my thoughts and humble suggestions on what else I believe we should consider as well.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: I am supportive of the direction taken and measures introduced to catalyse our economic transformation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: I also appreciate the measures aimed at strengthening our own capabilities so that we will not, as much as possible, be at the mercy of external elements such as foreign manpower.

sections.label: Innovation in social sector
sections.summary: The Budget's emphasis on innovation and partnership is correct and timely and should apply to the social sector.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: The Budget's emphasis on innovation and partnership is correct and timely, and these should apply to the social sector as well.

sections.label: Community Networks for Seniors pilot
sections.summary: Piloting Community Networks for Seniors is announced, differing from family-based or institutional eldercare and helping achieve ageing in place.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Every one of us has to do our part.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: I am therefore excited by the announcement of piloting Community Networks for Seniors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: This is not exactly an innovation in terms of how we care for our elderly, though it is different from the traditional approach of family-based or institutional-based eldercare.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: It can also help us achieve the vision of "ageing in place".

sections.label: Technologies for elderly home care
sections.summary: Examples include intelligent homes detecting anomalies, assistive technologies for bedridden elderly, and an integrated digital platform for requesting home care.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: For example, build intelligent homes that can detect anomalies so that designated neighbours or Social Service Officers (SSO) can be alerted to intervene and help in a timely manner; make use of assistive technologies, controlled by speech or eye movements or mind, to enable a bedridden elderly to move around at home and execute daily living activities; make available an integrated digital platform with schedule optimising capabilities that allows the elderly to request for home care or any other social services or support in the comfort of their own homes without having to worry about what numbers to dial or which organisations have or do not have the services they need.

sections.label: First Step Grant for children
sections.summary: The First Step Grant ensures every Singaporean child has a minimum of $3,000 in their CDA from birth.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: The First Step Grant is another step in this direction, given that some 5% of parents cannot even afford to deposit a cent in their children's Child Development Account (CDA).

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Hence, this grant ensures that any Singaporean child will have a minimum of $3,000 in their CDA from the moment they are born.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Earlier on, hon Member, Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin, made the impassionate call for this to be given to all kids, regardless of the marital status of the parents.

sections.label: Pregnancy and career progression
sections.summary: Working mothers who are PMEs in MNCs shared that pregnancy can hold back career progression or promotion for one year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Some working mothers, who are PMEs in MNCs, shared with me that whenever a woman becomes pregnant, her career progression or promotion can get held back for one year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: While they understand that the firms have to fairly reward others who inevitably have to step in to cover their duties during the downtime following birth, the opportunity costs are considerable.

sections.label: Income tax relief cap
sections.summary: The $80,000 personal income tax relief cap almost only hits working mothers from mid-management and higher, who feel singled out.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: The personal income tax relief cap of $80,000 almost only hits working mothers, specifically those from mid-management and higher.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Quite a few of the working mothers who are affected have reached out to me to express their unhappiness.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Rightly or wrongly, these working mothers feel singled out because their male contemporaries are generally unaffected by this move.

sections.label: Working mothers affected
sections.summary: The Government had known that the people affected are mostly working mothers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Surely, the Government had known that the people affected are mostly working mothers.

sections.label: Refining Work-Life Grant
sections.summary: The Government is asked whether it could refine the Work-Life Grant to encourage employers to tap on technology so face-time at work is less necessary.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: For example, could the Government refine the current Work-Life Grant to encourage employers to tap on technology more so that face-time at work is less necessary?

sections.label: Healthcare spending and schemes
sections.summary: The speaker says it is our responsibility to look after them, citing the 3M approach, MediShield Life and enhanced CHAS.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: Now, it is our responsibility to look after them.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: I know we have managed to keep our healthcare spending over the decades on the lower end with our unique 3M approach – MediShield, MediSave and MediFund.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: I sat on the MediFund Board for several years and I know how it has helped so many of our people.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: We have improved MediShield to MediShield Life last year, providing universal healthcare insurance coverage for all Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: The Community Health Assistance Scheme (CHAS) was also enhanced in 2014 to help Singaporeans with outpatient primary care services in the private sector.

sections.label: Silver Support Scheme help
sections.summary: The speaker is glad more is being done to help the less fortunate with the Silver Support Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: To those that are not so fortunate, I am glad we are doing more to help with the Silver Support Scheme.

sections.label: Seniors aged 60 and above
sections.summary: As of June 2015, there are 670,000 Singaporeans aged 60 and above.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: As of June 2015, there are 670,000 Singaporeans aged 60 and above.

sections.label: Meeting Mdm Loke
sections.summary: Last Christmas at a PCF eldercare centre, the speaker met a new client, Mdm Loke, aged 72.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: Last Christmas, I was at our PCF eldercare centre, and I met a new client, Mdm Loke, aged 72.

sections.label: Senior learning and community engagement
sections.summary: A participant felt better after joining a programme, and the coordinator taught her mathematics, prompting a call for seniors to stay engaged in the community.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: After a few weeks of participation, she began to feel better and did not need to apply any plasters or Page: 12 continue her rehabilitation therapy.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: As she did not have the opportunity to attend school, the programme coordinator decided to teach her mathematics.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: This conversation left a strong impression on me on the joy of learning − that we should and can continue to learn at all ages.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: We should look at how we can harness SkillsFuture to roll out interesting courses in our Community Clubs to keep our seniors engaged.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: To our seniors, I say, "You can retire from work but please do not retire from our community".

sections.label: Budget 2016 targeted business support
sections.summary: Budget 2016 took a targeted approach, deferring levy increases for Marine and Process Sectors and keeping work permit levies unchanged for Manufacturing.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: We must continue to work together to continue to give this hope to all Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: I am encouraged that Budget 2016 has taken a more targeted and differentiated approach, making deliberate and calibrated measures to address both near-term concerns facing our businesses, especially SMEs, and the longer-term challenges of restructuring.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The deferment of the levy increases for the Marine and Process Sectors and having work permit levies for Manufacturing remain unchanged for another year are a welcome move and a recognition of the challenges that these businesses face.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The Industry Transformation Programme is targeted and sector-focused to support SMEs to innovate, scale up, as well as to seek new market growths.

sections.label: Career Support Programme for mature PMEs
sections.summary: The Career Support Programme, since October 2015, gives employers wage support for hiring mature Singaporean PMEs jobless for at least six months.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The Career Support Programme (CSP), which has been in place since October 2015, encourages employers to employ mature Singaporean PMEs by providing wage support to employers for the first year when they hire PMEs who have been looking for jobs for at least six months in mid-level jobs that pay at least $4,000 and up to $7,000 a month.

sections.label: Targeted approach to workforce skills
sections.summary: A more targeted approach with organisations and businesses is urged to address changing job demands and grow skills, with plans for a Singapore Core.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: So, in the same way of taking a targeted approach to help companies restructure, we should take a more targeted approach with organisations and businesses to address the changing job demands and growing the skills base for these organisations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: I encourage the Government to do more and have clear plans on developing a Singapore Core in the workforce.

sections.label: Lean Enterprise Development Scheme for SMEs
sections.summary: The LED programme, effected October 2015, recognises transitional manpower adjustments to help companies restructure and undertake transformational projects for technology skills.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Along the lines of the Lean Enterprise Development Scheme (LED) for SMEs that was effected in October 2015, in how they can help businesses restructure to be a more manpower-lean organisation, the LED programme recognises the transitional manpower adjustments to enable Page: 14 companies to embark on transformational projects to redevelop and provide for these technology skills required.

sections.label: Business Grants Portal launch
sections.summary: The launch of the Business Grants Portal is described as a good first step.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: A good first step is the launch of the Business Grants Portal.

sections.label: Application rejected as unqualified
sections.summary: A woman chased her application and was told it was not submitted because she did not qualify.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: After we have made the application, then we will know." She had to continue to chase them and, finally, she was told that they did not submit her application because she did not qualify.

sections.label: Feedback on middle-income retirees
sections.summary: Residents' feedback called for doing more for middle-income retirees, triggered by expectations on the Silver Support Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Feedback I received from residents, not just specifically from this Budget, but from the dialogues and the chats I had, was the need to do more for middle-income retirees.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: And I believe this sentiment was triggered because of the expectations on the Silver Support Scheme.

sections.label: Housing type in means testing
sections.summary: Minister Heng noted difficulty operationalising the scheme using three criteria, while some say housing type ignores cash-poor, asset-rich retirees.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Minister Heng himself did share the difficulty in assessing and operationalising the scheme effectively and hence, the use of the three criteria in combination.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: But some feel that the use of housing type, like other means-tested schemes, does not recognise that retired middle-income seniors may need support as they are asset-rich because of their housing type but are cash-poor.

sections.label: Building capability and competence
sections.summary: Budget 2016 stresses building people's capability and competence so Singapore can deliver results and earn trust.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: A key tenet of Budget 2016 is the need to continue to build capability and competence in our people.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Character is necessary for trust to exist in any circumstance but trust also requires the ability to deliver results and impact.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Therefore, it is important, whether it is SkillsFuture or this whole investment in innovation, whether it is at the individual or the organisation level, we have to ensure that if we, as Singapore, want to continue to earn that trust, we need to build that competence and capability to be able to deliver that while we maintain the character of this country.

sections.label: People as only resource
sections.summary: People are Singapore's only resource and it is a small nation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: People are our only resource and we are a small nation.

sections.label: Budget 2016 and SG100
sections.summary: In his Budget speech, the speaker said Budget 2016 begins the journey towards SG100.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In my Budget speech, I said that Budget 2016 is the beginning of our journey towards SG100.

sections.label: Budget support for SMEs
sections.summary: The Budget addresses the need to grow the economy and is tilted towards supporting over 180,000 SMEs, which account for nearly two-thirds of employment.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: This is a timely reminder of why we need to grow the economy.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: This is what the Budget seeks to address and this is also why we have set up the Committee on the Future Economy.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Indeed, this Budget is tilted towards supporting SMEs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: There are over 180,000 SMEs, accounting for nearly two-thirds of our employment.

sections.label: Nurturing spirit of enterprise
sections.summary: A common thread in helping firms and workers is to nurture, celebrate and reinforce the spirit of enterprise, aiming for long-term vitality rather than short-term fixes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Listening to all your comments, however, there is a common thread running through how we can help firms and workers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: This common thread is to nurture, celebrate and reinforce the spirit of enterprise and not undermine it even as we provide support – to go for long-term vitality and not short-term fixes.

sections.label: Helping viable firms survive
sections.summary: Supporting the spirit of enterprise includes helping viable firms survive cyclical weakness so precious capabilities are not lost, with the Budget calibrated to address cyclical concerns without impeding restructuring.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: One way of supporting this spirit of enterprise is to make sure that viable firms can survive this period of cyclical weakness.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Otherwise, we lose precious capabilities that are difficult to rebuild later.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Page: 19 This is why this year's Budget is carefully calibrated to address cyclical concerns without impeding restructuring.

sections.label: Rental costs declined in 2015
sections.summary: Rental costs declined over 2015, with retail, office and industrial rents falling by 4.1%, 6.5% and 2.1% respectively.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In fact, rental costs have declined over 2015.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Retail, office and industrial rents fell by 4.1%, 6.5% and 2.1% respectively.

sections.label: Five Budget support aims
sections.summary: The Budget seeks to help entrepreneurial firms scale up and internationalise, support automation, encourage innovation, revitalise heartlands, and provide broad support to SMEs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In this Budget, we seek to one, help entrepreneurial firms scale up and internationalise; two, support automation to build capacity; three, encourage innovation; four, support our shops through the revitalisation of heartlands; and five, provide a broad range of support to SMEs so that everyone has the opportunity to upgrade, to raise capability and to compete.

sections.label: PIC objectives and SME productivity
sections.summary: The PIC has largely achieved its objectives, with 102,000 companies benefiting as at January 2016, and around 90% of SMEs taking steps to increase productivity.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding some of the reports, let me clarify that the PIC has, in fact, largely achieved its objectives.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: As at January 2016, 102,000 companies have benefited from PIC.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: This is about 70% of all active companies in IRAS' records for the Year of Assessment 2014.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Page: 21 Today, around 90% of SMEs are taking steps to increase their productivity, according to a survey by the Singapore Chinese Chamber of Commerce and Industry (SCCCI).

sections.label: Consultation consensus on implementation
sections.summary: Consultations reached consensus that this is the best way forward, and implementation will require strong partnerships, with trust among firms, unions and the Government.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Based on our consultations, the consensus at this point is that this is the best way forward.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Mr Liang Eng Hwa rightly pointed out, together with several others, that implementation will be key.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: As industry needs are complex, it will require strong partnerships.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: But we have the advantage of trust among firms, unions and the Government.

sections.label: Robotic cutting and staff training
sections.summary: A new robotic cutting system raised cutting productivity 18 times, and trained staff got 10% to 20% higher pay and an in-house robotics team.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: First, they adopted a new robotic cutting system, which increased the productivity of the cutting process by 18 times.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Third, they trained their staff to operate the new machines, increased the pay of trained staff by 10% to 20%, and built an in-house robotics team.

sections.label: Wavelength Opto-Electronic laser equipment
sections.summary: Help was given to Wavelength Opto-Electronic, an SME maker of infrared optic components, to develop miniaturised laser equipment, raising annual sales over 20%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: For example, they helped Wavelength Opto-Electronic, an SME manufacturer of infrared optic components, develop a first-of-its-kind miniaturised laser equipment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: This new system helped to grade the quality of the products and the company's annual sales have increased by over 20% since.

sections.label: Industry Transformation Programme coordination
sections.summary: Under the Industry Transformation Programme, a Government agency will be appointed to coordinate efforts and develop a Transformation Map for each sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: SBF aims to reach 30,000 SMEs by 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: In 2013, the Ministry of Trade and Industry launched the SME Talent Programme to help match SMEs with students.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Since its launch, around 50 organisations are on board and more than 350 scholarships have been awarded.

sections.label: SG-Innovate and pervasive innovation
sections.summary: SG-Innovate was set up to connect innovators to money, mentors, markets and R&D experts, with innovation needed in all sectors and firms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: To do that, we need to connect the many dots.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: That is why we set up SG-Innovate – to connect innovators to smart money, mentors, markets and experts in the R&D area.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: The thrust of my Budget speech is that innovation must be pervasive and must be present in all sectors of the economy and in all firms, including SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: That is what I meant by "there is no sunset industry, only sunset thinking", a point which Mr Thomas Chua elaborated on very well.

sections.label: China rebalancing economy layoffs
sections.summary: China is rebalancing from heavy industries to services and may lay off over 1.5 million workers from coal and steel alone.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: China is rebalancing its economy from heavy industries to services and may lay off over 1.5 million workers from the coal and steel industries alone.

sections.label: Unemployment, participation and median income
sections.summary: At end-2015 unemployment was 2.9% for residents and 3% for citizens, labour force participation rose to 68.3%, and real median income grew 3% yearly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: At the end of 2015, the unemployment rate was 2.9% for residents and 3% for citizens, which most economists would regard as close to full employment, as there is always some degree of frictional unemployment in any economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: The labour force participation rate has risen from 66.2% in 2010 to 68.3% in 2015, which is higher than the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) average.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: The OECD average is about 60%, so we have a very high labour force participation rate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: And importantly, real median income has grown by 3% per annum over the last five years.

sections.label: Productivity and 24-hour operations
sections.summary: As a result of this innovation, productivity increased four times and operations run 24 hours a day.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: As a result of this innovation, productivity increased four times and operations run 24 hours a day!

sections.label: WSQ and part-time programme enrolment
sections.summary: In 2015, over 260,000 residents took WSQ courses and 22,000 enrolled in part-time diploma, post-diploma and degree programmes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: In 2015, over 260,000 residents took up WSQ courses and 22,000 were enrolled in part-time diploma, post-diploma and degree-level programmes in our polytechnics and publicly funded universities.

sections.label: SkillsFuture online learning portal
sections.summary: An online individualised learning portal for career and lifelong learning planning will launch in phases from 2017.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Under SkillsFuture, we are developing an online, individualised learning portal for individuals to plan their careers and lifelong learning.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: The portal will be launched in phases starting from 2017.

sections.label: Adapt and Grow Programme
sections.summary: The Adapt and Grow Programme provides wage support and reskilling help, with PMET outreach expected to more than double from 2,000 to over 4,000 yearly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Besides employment and training assistance, wage support is also provided in some cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: This year's Budget builds on these programmes with the launch of the Adapt and Grow Programme, which will provide support for more Singaporeans to reskill and gain employment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: As I mentioned in the Budget Statement, we expect to more than double the current outreach for PMETs from 2,000 per year to over 4,000.

sections.label: Support for low-income families
sections.summary: Low-income families pay low childcare and kindergarten fees, and eligible children receive KidStart support, Baby Bonus, MediSave, CDA grants and school subsidies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Low-income families pay as little as $3 a month for childcare and $1 a month for kindergarten.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: The KidStart pilot will draw together Government and community resources to provide these children with learning, developmental and health support, even before they enter school.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: For each eligible child, parents may receive a Baby Bonus Cash Gift of $8,000 or $10,000, depending on birth order; the MediSave grant for newborns of $4,000; and now, the new Child Development Account (CDA) First Step grant of $3,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: In total, parents of eligible children receive between $15,000 and $17,000 in the first 18 months of their child's birth.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: A child who attends primary and secondary school also receives around $11,000 a year in educational subsidies.

sections.label: Subsidies and CPF interest for seniors
sections.summary: Government subsidies cover seniors' healthcare, CPF pays extra interest from age 55, and WIS supplements low-income workers up to 30% of income.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: These have been complemented by increased Government subsidies for seniors across all healthcare settings, including subsidies for MediShield Life premiums, GP clinics via CHAS, and for eldercare.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: We also pay extra interest on CPF, with the first $30,000 in CPF earning up to 6% interest from the age of 55.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: With the past enhancements, WIS is now a significant supplement for low-income workers of up to 30% of their income.

sections.label: Government transfers per retiree
sections.summary: For those in 3-room and larger HDB flats up to Executive Apartments, Government transfers averaged around $5,000 per retiree in 2015.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Even if Page: 30 we consider only those living in 3-room and larger HDB flats – up to Executive Apartments, on average, this worked out to around $5,000 in Government transfers per retiree in 2015.

sections.label: Silver Support supplement
sections.summary: Silver Support is a modest supplement targeted at the bottom 20% of seniors, with some support extended to the next 10%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: First, let me reiterate that Silver Support is a modest but meaningful supplement targeted at the bottom 20% of seniors, with some support extended to the next 10%.

sections.label: Pioneer Generation Package outreach
sections.summary: Over one-and-a-half years, 250,000 Pioneers, or 60%, were reached to explain the Pioneer Generation Package and MediShield Life benefits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Over the past one-and-a-half years, they have reached out to 250,000 Pioneers, or 60%, to explain the benefits of the Pioneer Generation Package (PGP) and MediShield Life.

sections.label: Social Service Offices access
sections.summary: Residents can approach 24 Social Service Offices, and with Family Service Centres, 95% of those needing help have access within two kilometres.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Today, they can approach 24 Social Service Offices (SSOs) across the island for assistance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Page: 32 Along with Family Service Centres (FSCs), 95% of the island's residents who need help have access to it within two kilometres of where they live or work.

sections.label: Expanding Social Service Net

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: The third move is integrating assistance from Government agencies and VWOs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: We are expanding the Social Service Net (SSNet), our integrated information sharing and case management system that links MSF with other Government agencies, as well as VWOs.

sections.label: Care and Share matching grants

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Over the past two years, the Government provided $500 million in matching grants for the Care and Share Movement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: The Business and IPC Partnership Scheme (BIPS) pilot is designed to support more partnerships between businesses and Institutions of a Public Character (IPC) and encourage employee volunteerism.

sentences.text: Today, one in eight Singaporeans is aged 65 and above.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat

sections.label: Fairness and progressive personal income tax
sections.summary: A cap was imposed to make personal income tax more progressive, with 99% of tax resident individuals claiming reliefs fully.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: We have to maintain fairness between different groups of taxpayers, in particular, between those who earn Page: 35 more and those who earn less.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: We have thus imposed a cap to make our personal income tax more progressive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Ninety-nine percent of tax resident individuals can continue to claim their reliefs fully.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: For those claiming Working Mother's Child Relief (WMCR), even with the cap, nine in 10 of those claiming WMCR are not affected.

sections.label: Committee on the Future Economy
sections.summary: The Committee on the Future Economy will keep looking ahead to plot the road for a vibrant, strong future economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: The Committee on the Future Economy will continue to look towards the horizon, to plot out what we can of the road ahead, so we can take the right steps for a vibrant, strong future economy that creates good opportunities for our people.

sections.label: Investing in SkillsFuture
sections.summary: The passage states that for this reason, investing in SkillsFuture will continue.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: For this reason, we will keep investing in SkillsFuture.

sections.label: Budget 2016 resilience and partnership
sections.summary: Budget 2016 sought to strengthen resilience and bring out the instinct for care and partnership in all.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: By giving and sharing, that is how we transform our world and how we may ourselves be transformed for the better.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: We have sought in Budget 2016 to strengthen our resilience and to bring out the natural instinct for care and partnership in all of us.

sentences.text: Earlier, in his round-up speech, he acknowledged that Singaporeans are worried about their jobs, and he mentioned that the Government was reviewing how it could better support people who lose their jobs through some difficulties, including perhaps reviewing the retrenchment benefits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: As I have said, we now have 15 different types of tax reliefs.

So, I would urge Mr Low to read my speech carefully and perhaps also to read the reports and discuss with fellow Members here what they took away from the speech.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat

sections.label: Connecting SMEs to innovation hubs

sentences.text: What are the plans that the Government has to connect these SMEs to the innovation hubs so that they can draw on the innovation expertise, the research that is coming out of NUS and NTU?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I understand that SPRING has the Centres of Innovation where these SMEs can connect to polytechnics and certain research institutes.

sections.label: SPRING schemes and Automation Support Package

sentences.text: First of all, I mentioned SPRING's schemes: we have the Innovation and Capability Voucher and the Capability Development Grant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: And in this Budget, I devoted a lot of time to talk about the Automation Support Package.

sentences.text: The quality control for SkillsFuture would be done by the MOE Higher Education Division, MOM and WDA.
